brief: Build plant-products/CHED-PP as a SIBLING SET of live-animals inside trade-imports-animals-frontend — a new sets/plant-products/ tree served CO-RESIDENTLY with live-animals FROM ONE NODE PROCESS under SYMMETRIC MOUNTS (live-animals MIGRATES from the root to /live-animals; plant-products mounts at /plant-products; neither set owns / , which becomes a server-wide 302 to /live-animals) rather than a standalone CDP application — plus a new /plant-products/ REST surface and Mongo schema in trade-imports-animals-backend, plus the matching migration and plant-products coverage in trade-imports-animals-tests. THIS PROGRAMME SPANS THREE REPOS, not two: trade-imports-animals-frontend (the sets, the platform seams, the per-set URL namespace), trade-imports-animals-backend (the /plant-products/ schema, REST surface and copy idempotency) and trade-imports-animals-tests (the workspace E2E/a11y/cross-browser suite, which is migrated onto the new URLs by pp-059 and then grown a full plant-products lane by pp-060..pp-067). All three carry the SAME branch name, spike/trace-to-requirements, per CLAUDE.md rule 2. Sam's ruling R3 (2026-08-01) REVERSES the earlier boot-time SERVED_SET one-set-per-process switch: the L1-L4 architecture was explicitly designed to be set-agnostic (L2 never imports a set, sets arrive via the L1 configure* seams, dep-cruiser enforces the boundary), so the blocker was never the design but two implementation details — module-level single-slot singletons behind every configure* seam, and a hardcoded global URL namespace in shared/paths.js. Sam's ruling R7 (2026-08-01, later session) then REVERSES FD-16, the asymmetric root mount: both sets sit under their own prefix, live-animals' URLs change, and the tests repo is migrated with them. The platform work that delivers both is IN SCOPE and scheduled in m0: pp-056 (P-9, set-context + every seam keyed by set), pp-057 (P-10, the symmetric per-set URL namespace and the live-animals URL migration) and pp-058 (P-11, the setId-first + symmetric-mount tripwire), with pp-059 migrating the tests repo in lockstep with pp-057, pp-006 registering both gateways in one process and pp-011 proving co-residency end to end via test:features:all. Ruling R6 puts the recipe first: pp-053 authors src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md BEFORE any plant-products file exists and the scaffold increments follow it verbatim. Ruling R4 lands copy idempotency (pp-054 backend, pp-055 frontend) in m0, matching the live-animals implementation exactly, so the Copy button cannot ship without it. Ruling R8 puts the tests repo in scope as a first-class delivery lane rather than a repo that merely must not break. Everything is grounded in the trace-mined CHED-PP requirements at workareas/shared/trace-requirements/ched-pp/ (39 pages, 354 field rows, 310 validation messages; 8 conflict rulings closed by Sam on 2026-07-18) and in the Phase-C scaffold plan at frontend-plan/SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md. Pass 1 covers m0-m4: the backend schema and its tests, the add-a-set recipe, the platform seams that let two sets be served at once, the symmetric URL migration across frontend and tests, the set scaffold and its records adapter, reference-data fixtures, and the MANUAL, OWN-ORG, HAPPY-PATH journey from the import-type entry filter through origin, purpose, the depth-3 commodity collection, additional details, transport, goods movement, contacts, accompanying-document metadata, traders and consignor, to review, declaration and confirmation, with a 12-spoke task-list hub and a notifications dashboard — each milestone matched by its own tests-repo increment. m5 carries six buildable-in-the-tail stubs (CSV commodity branch, CUC billing, consignor address-book search, draft lifecycle delete/amend/copy, the Article 72 no-op rule hook, the auth stub), one planned tests-repo lifecycle increment (pp-067) and five deferred stubs (the whole delegated-authority ownership/visibility/auto-population layer and its two pages, file bytes plus antivirus, and the cloning front door) — none of the eleven stubs has been planned, and each must be planned before it is built. Integrations are stubbed throughout pass 1: fixed signed-in user and single stubbed organisation, allow-all permissions, fixture reference data, always-low risk, no certificate PDF, no Dynamics, no TRACES, no Notify. Post-submission is out of scope entirely.

scopeDecisions.topic: Architecture — sibling set, not a standalone app
scopeDecisions.decision: NEW for this backlog, supersedes the source inc-001..inc-003 assumption. plant-products is a SIBLING SET under src/server/app/sets/plant-products/ in the existing trade-imports-animals-frontend, not a new CDP application. The source's 'scaffold a CDP app' (inc-001), 'Mongo persistence spine' (inc-002) and 'session/routing spine' (inc-003) are re-interpreted as pp-007 (set scaffold + L1 gateway), pp-008 (set-owned records adapter over the backend REST surface) and pp-009 (set flow/session spine).

scopeDecisions.topic: Architecture — CO-RESIDENCY: both sets served side by side from ONE Node process (REVERSES the boot-time set switch)
scopeDecisions.decision: REVERSED 2026-08-01. live-animals and plant-products MUST be servable side by side FROM ONE NODE PROCESS. Under R7 the mounts are SYMMETRIC: every set is registered under '/' + setId, so live-animals serves at /live-animals and plant-products at /plant-products, and one routes.js barrel registers both gateways. There is no SERVED_SET env var, no boot-time selector and no one-set-per-process rule — those are deleted, not merely unused (a vestigial env var would invite a future reader to think a set still had to be picked). The platform work that makes co-residency real is IN SCOPE and scheduled in m0: pp-056 (P-9 — shared/set-context.js, every configure* seam keyed by set through AsyncLocalStorage, with an FD-17 sole-registered-set fallback so the existing live-animals suite stays green with no test edits beyond the mechanical cookie-accessor rename), pp-057 (P-10 — the symmetric per-set URL namespace: setBase(), the route-shape vs link-builder split, the per-set journey cookie path, the enumerated live-animals URL migration, the '/' redirect and the signout hoist; shared/paths.js IS changed in pass 1) and pp-058 (P-11 — the setId-first AND symmetric-mount convention tripwire, no-set-singletons.test.js). pp-059 migrates the tests repo onto the new URLs in lockstep with pp-057. pp-006 makes both gateways register in one process and is where co-residency.test.js is born; pp-011 adds test:features:all (both Playwright projects, one server) as the E2E-level co-residency proof.
scopeDecisions.reasoning: Sam's reasoning: the L1-L4 architecture was EXPLICITLY DESIGNED to be set-agnostic — L2 never imports a set, sets arrive via the L1 configure* seams, and dep-cruiser enforces the boundary at error severity. The blocker was therefore never the design, it was two implementation details: (a) every configure* seam stores its value in a module-level single-slot singleton, and (b) shared/paths.js hardcodes a global URL namespace. Keying the seams by set removes (a) and namespacing the URLs removes (b). A boot-time switch would have entrenched an implementation limit as though it were an architectural one.
scopeDecisions.supersedes: The headless Phase-C ruling of 2026-07-31, now VOID: 'One set per Node process, selected at boot by SERVED_SET (values live-animals (default) | plant-products; FD-1). routes.js becomes the selector and is the ONLY reader of the env var; an unknown value is a loud boot failure. Co-residency (per-set URL BASE, keyed singletons, two sets in one process) is explicitly OUT of scope, which is why shared/paths.js is unchanged in pass 1 (FD-4).' SIBLING-SET-PLAN FD-1, FD-2 and FD-4 go void with it. The asymmetric-mount half of the round-2 position (FD-16, live-animals keeps the root and only plant-products is prefixed) is separately void under R7 — see SD-17.

scopeDecisions.topic: Copy idempotency matches the live-animals implementation exactly, on both sides, before the Copy button ships
scopeDecisions.decision: Copy is idempotent on an Idempotency-Key, implemented EXACTLY as live-animals already implements it, on both sides, and sequenced BEFORE the Copy button ships (pp-045, which now carries pp-054 and pp-055 in dependsOn). BACKEND (pp-054): Idempotency-Key as a REQUIRED @RequestHeader on POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies, blank rejected with a bad-request 'Idempotency-Key must not be blank'; the copy carries copyIdempotencyKey with a UNIQUE PARTIAL index over string-typed values only; the service looks the key up first and RETURNS THE EXISTING COPY on a repeat, re-checking after a DuplicateKeyException. FRONTEND (pp-055): a randomUUID() minted per RENDERED copy action, carried in a hidden idempotencyKey input, sent as the Idempotency-Key header by the real records adapter, mirrored by the stub's dedupe key, with records-port contract tests pinning 'one new draft per idempotency key' and 'copy idempotency scoped to the source reference'. THE ONE TRANSPOSITION: live-animals implements this on the FULFILMENT resource (FulfilmentController / FulfilmentService / Fulfilment.copyIdempotencyKey), whereas the plant-products design puts /copies on the NOTIFICATION resource — transpose the PATTERN, not the code. Because pp-045 (which renders the Copy button) is an unplanned m5 stub under SD-12, the rendering half is ENFORCED rather than built now: both plant adapters throw on a missing key, so any future Copy button that forgets to mint one fails in unit tests, and the four-rule rendering contract is written into the set charter where pp-045's planner will read it. A Copy action arriving without both increments is a build-loop halt.

scopeDecisions.topic: SYMMETRIC MOUNTS — every set sits under '/' + setId, live-animals' URLs change, and the tests repo moves with them
scopeDecisions.decision: R7 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session) REVERSES FD-16. There is NO asymmetry: both sets mount under their own prefix — live-animals at /live-animals, plant-products at /plant-products — registered by Hapi's plugin routes.prefix, with route shapes declared PREFIX-FREE and byte-identical between the sets and only the per-request link builders resolving setBase(). live-animals' URLs MOVE (dashboard / -> /live-animals, create /notifications -> /live-animals/notifications, hub /notifications/{journeyId} -> /live-animals/notifications/{journeyId}, page /notifications/{journeyId}/{slug} -> /live-animals/notifications/{journeyId}/{slug}) and that churn is ACCEPTED. WHAT SERVES '/' (FD-18): a server-wide 302 redirect to /live-animals, declared with server.route in router.js alongside health and signout and NEVER inside a gateway, so it never enters a set context and never appears in either set's allRoutes. Chosen over a set-picker page and over a 404 because OIDC is the binding constraint — auth/controller.js falls back to '/' in five places and getSafeRedirect only permits relative paths, so a 404 at '/' would break sign-in for anyone arriving without a stored redirect, while a picker page needs new copy in two locales, a11y baselines and a design decision nobody has made. 302, not 301, because a 301 is cached indefinitely by browsers and would be painful to unpick when a picker page eventually replaces it (the recorded upgrade path for a third set). NO legacy /notifications/* compatibility shim: there are no external bookmarks to honour at this stage and a shim would have to guess which set a bare journey id belongs to, so a stale deep link 404s by design. THE SIGNOUT HOIST (FD-19): router.js today pushes signout into the SAME register array as live-animals, so adding the prefix would silently move /signout to /live-animals/signout — it registers fine, nothing fails, and the OIDC sign-out leg just breaks in the browser; signout is hoisted into its own unprefixed register and pinned by a router-suite case. THE ACCEPTANCE BAR THAT DIED WITH FD-16: round 2 asserted that 'every existing URL assertion passes UNEDITED — that is the proof the root mount is a no-op'. That bar is WRONG in both directions under R7 — zero spec edits would mean the mount did nothing, and an assertion that survives the migration unchanged is an assertion that never tested the prefix. It is replaced by an explicit, ENUMERATED migration (SIBLING-SET-PLAN §4.6 A-D, executed as a ticked checklist file by file, not as a hunt) proven by UPDATED, FRONT-ANCHORED assertions in both the frontend suite (pp-057) and the tests repo (pp-059). CROSS-REPO PAIRING: pp-057 and pp-059 are a pair on the same branch name; between the two commits the workspace E2E suite is red BY CONSTRUCTION and nothing may be sequenced between them.
scopeDecisions.reasoning: Sam's words: 'this stuff is still in development, refactoring live-animals is fine — have them match up; changing URLs if required, just make sure to update the -tests repo as well.' The engineering reason symmetry is SAFER and not merely tidier: with live-animals at prefix '', a DOUBLED prefix (setBase() used where a route shape was wanted) and a DROPPED prefix (a route shape used where a link was wanted) produce the SAME correct-looking string for live-animals, because '' + '/notifications' is '/notifications' either way. That whole bug class could therefore only surface on the plant side, in code the live-animals suite never exercises — and the 'every live-animals assertion passes unedited' bar would have actively certified it as fine. With neither set at '', both mistakes fail visibly for BOTH sets on the first request. Symmetry costs one enumerated migration once; asymmetry costs a permanent special case in shared/paths.js, in registerSetMount and in add-a-set.md, plus a hidden bug class and a permanent 'the incumbent is different' fact in every future planner's head.
scopeDecisions.supersedes: SIBLING-SET-PLAN FD-16 (asymmetric root mount — 'live-animals stays root-mounted at / with its URLs unchanged; only plant-products is prefixed') and every acceptance bar derived from it, notably pp-057/P-10's 'every existing URL assertion passes UNEDITED' and the 'live-animals still served at / with byte-identical URLs' clause of the two-sided verification rule.

scopeDecisions.topic: trade-imports-animals-tests is a first-class delivery lane, not a repo that merely must not break
scopeDecisions.decision: R8 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session) puts the tests repo IN SCOPE with real increments. THE GAP THIS CLOSES, stated honestly: across the round-2 backlog's 58 increments only pp-053 and pp-057 mentioned repos/trade-imports-animals-tests at all, and only to assert it should not break — there were ZERO increments adding plant-products coverage to it. Sam asked outright 'have you got it in the plan to update the -tests repo with all the plants stuff?' and the answer was no. NINE tests-repo increments now carry the lane: pp-059 (cut spike/trace-to-requirements in that repo — it currently sits on spike/EUDPA-288-model-retrofit, and CLAUDE.md rule 2 requires cross-repo branches to share a name — then execute the enumerated URL migration onto /live-animals, paired with pp-057), pp-060 (the per-set tree and per-set Playwright projects — the symmetry half of R7, a pure git mv with an identical test count as its acceptance bar), pp-061 (m1: the plant-products API client, domain models and Mongo seed fixtures), pp-062 (m2 coverage), pp-063 (m3 depth-3 commodities coverage), pp-064 (m4 pages plus hub/CYA feature specs), pp-065 (the whole-journey E2E, cross-browser smoke and the co-residency spec), pp-066 (the a11y suite, mirroring the live-animals specs file for file) and pp-067 (m5 lifecycle coverage via API seed). Each sits at the END of its milestone so it asserts against pages that already exist. The repo's own scripts govern its verification ladder — typecheck, lint, format:check, test (which shells bin/assert-stack.sh first), test:local, test:a11y, test:cross-browser, test:docker-compose — and NOTHING from the frontend package.json applies there. Its work is committed on ITS branch, in ITS repo, never from the workspace root. The workspace stack must run in dev mode (run-stack.sh -d -b spike/trace-to-requirements) for any of it, or a Dockerhub :latest image that predates the mount will fail every migrated assertion in a way that looks like the edits are wrong.

The reason to keep separate files is now plain readability and independent failure attribution (FD-10 as revised), and the mechanics are simpler than before — FD-17's sole-registered-set fallback means a clone composing exactly ONE set resolves currentSetId() with no context plumbing at all. What changes mechanically in every clone is that each configure*/buildDispatch call takes setId as its FIRST argument; a clone that needs withSetContext is composing more than one set and is wrong. The one file that legitimately holds explicit set context is co-residency.test.js, which is not a clone. The load-bearing warning survives untouched: never compute a set-derived value at module load.

sequencingNotes: HARD GATE 1 — pp-012 (P-7 depth-3 nested-collection characterisation test) must be GREEN before ANY m3 work starts. It composes a synthetic 3-deep manifest as an L2 fixture and exercises grouped-binding registration at depth 3, appendEntryAt/updateEntryAt/removeEntryAt, per-instance scope and wipe, collection-complete rollup and dispatch coverage inheritance. GREEN means the m3 commodity increments proceed on the platform as-is; ANY RED raises a NEW platform work item that must land before pp-021. Every m3 increment (pp-021..pp-028) carries pp-012 in dependsOn to make this unmissable.

HARD GATE 2 — pp-021 (commodity collection model extension) is a HALT-FOR-REVIEW model-extension gate, mirroring the source inc-012 nested-collection gate. The build loop must stop after pp-021, attach pp-012's characterisation evidence plus pp-021's own real-object characterisation suite, and wait for Sam's review of the depth-3 model before any commodity page (pp-022 onward collects it) proceeds.

THE m0 SPINE, IN ORDER (revised under R3/R6/R4/R7/R8): (0) pp-053 authors docs/add-a-set.md before any plant file exists — everything after it follows the recipe. (1) THE CO-RESIDENCY PLATFORM PHASE lands against LIVE-ANIMALS ALONE, which is what makes it verifiable: pp-056 (P-9, shared/set-context.js + every configure* seam keyed by set — the single largest platform increment in the programme), then pp-057 (P-10, the symmetric per-set URL namespace AND the enumerated live-animals URL migration). (2) pp-059 lands IMMEDIATELY after pp-057, in the tests repo, on the same branch name — the two are a cross-repo PAIR and the workspace E2E suite is red by construction between them; pp-060 follows with the per-set tree and projects. (3) pp-058 (P-11, the setId-first + symmetric-mount tripwire) lands next, still BEFORE the gateway split, so nothing from pp-006 onward can re-singleton a seam or reinstate a root mount. (4) pp-005 (P-1, obligation-source policy accessors) depends on pp-056 for obligationSet() being per-set; pp-006 (P-3, both gateways registering in one process, where co-residency.test.js is born) depends on pp-056 and pp-057. (5) pp-007 (set scaffold, booting co-resident at /plant-products) depends on pp-005, pp-006 and pp-053. Each platform step keeps the existing suite green: run npm test after every step of pp-056, not once at the end. Roll back a failed attempt with `git stash push -u`, never `reset --hard` + `clean -fd`.

Platform items land before the first obligation-bearing page (SIBLING-SET-PLAN §9 rule 2): pp-010 (dep-cruiser rules, cloned app-root suites, contract table) is a dependency of pp-018/pp-019/pp-020 because the policy seam and cloned contract table must exist for the first obligation to register cleanly.

TWO-SIDED VERIFICATION on every platform-touching increment: it is not enough that the plant set is green. Every increment that edits anything outside sets/plant-products/ (pp-053's reconciliation targets pp-056, pp-057, pp-058, pp-005, pp-006, pp-010, pp-011, and any platform work pp-012 raises) must also prove live-animals still works — the full existing live-animals suite green, no existing-suite test-count drop, and the dep-cruiser violations baseline NOT regenerated. WHAT THIS RULE NO LONGER SAYS (R7): it does NOT say 'live-animals still served at / with byte-identical URLs and no test edits'. From pp-057 onward live-animals is served at /live-animals and its URL assertions are DELIBERATELY edited; the bar there is an enumerated migration with updated, front-anchored assertions, not an untouched suite. Unchanged-URL wording survives only in increments that add plant-only files (e.g. pp-034), where it means 'unchanged by THIS increment' against the post-migration baseline. From pp-011 onward the ladder also runs test:features:all (both Playwright projects, ONE server) — the E2E-level proof that the two sets are genuinely co-resident rather than merely both present.

The gaps G-B..G-J mean several increments TRANSPOSE from live exemplars rather than follow a recipe: pp-008 (no records-adapter recipe), pp-009 (no entry-guard/opening-run authoring recipe), pp-017 and pp-039 (no flow-only-key recipe — transpose import-type-filter and declaration), pp-021/pp-025 (no depth-3 collection recipe), pp-029 (no create-the-hub-from-scratch recipe), pp-037 and pp-045 (no dashboard/lifecycle recipe), pp-038 (no check-answers-from-scratch recipe), pp-042 (no CSV-branch recipe anywhere) and the whole tests-repo lane pp-059..pp-067 (G-J — no 'add a set to the tests repo' recipe exists either; pp-060 establishes the convention and everything after it follows what pp-060 lands) must treat the gap text as first-class plan content and cite concrete live-animals files, not recipe steps. G-A is the exception and no longer applies at build time: under R6 the add-a-set recipe is WRITTEN FIRST by pp-053, so pp-056, pp-057, pp-006 and pp-007 follow a real recipe and reconcile the doc against what they ship.

Increment order in this array is topological and every dependsOn edge points EARLIER IN THE ARRAY, so the graph is acyclic by construction and the array can be walked front to back. Ids are deliberately out of numeric order in six places: pp-053 (the recipe) sits ahead of pp-003 because everything follows it; pp-054 (backend copy idempotency) sits with the backend cluster and pp-055 (its frontend half) immediately after pp-008, both far ahead of the pp-045 stub that renders the Copy button; pp-056/pp-057/pp-058 (the co-residency platform phase) sit ahead of pp-005/pp-006 because those now depend on the keyed seams; pp-059 and pp-060 (the tests-repo branch cut, URL migration and per-set tree) are spliced BETWEEN pp-057 and pp-058, because pp-057/pp-059 are a cross-repo pair that must land back to back and pp-058 only has to precede the gateway split; pp-010/pp-011 sit immediately after pp-007, ahead of pp-008/pp-009, because nearly every later increment runs the test:plant-products / test:features:* scripts they create; and each remaining tests-repo increment (pp-061, pp-062, pp-063, pp-064/pp-065/pp-066, pp-067) sits at the END of its milestone, after the pages it asserts against.

m1 reference data (pp-013..pp-016) all depend only on pp-007 and can run in any order or in parallel once the scaffold boots. The commodity-code + EPPO-species fixture (pp-014) is the ONE lookup that eventually goes real — ship a ~10-code fixture with species now.

The §2.3 flow sections array fixes the append order (start, origin, purpose, commodities, additional-details, transport, goods-movement, contacts, nominated-contacts, documents, parties, [billing], review); §2.1 fixes the canonical row ids and hub GROUPS. Rows for not-yet-built sections land WITH their section increment, not with pp-029.

c-004 (error-summary title) and c-014 (radio a11y) are NOT per-page blockers: every page ships the adopted GDS default and the sign-off is recorded once in this backlog, never re-litigated per increment.

Every page increment follows the add-a-page / add-a-section / add-a-collection recipes with the SIBLING-SET-PLAN §7 plant verification ladder substituted, and adds its valid-POST case to contract.plant-products.test.js (T-5 standing rule).

m5 is UNPLANNED except for pp-067. The eleven stubs pp-042..pp-052 must NOT be built from this backlog — each needs a planning pass first, and five of them are deferred out of first-pass scope altogether. The one planned m5 increment is pp-067, the tests-repo lifecycle suite; it depends on pp-045, so it cannot start until that stub has had its own planning pass and been built.

obligations[].id in this backlog IS the code-level obligation NAME as it will exist under sets/plant-products/obligations/** — path-safe camelCase (commodityLines, varietyClass, destinationAddressLine1, intendedForFinalUsers). It is never a slug and never kebab-case. Kebab strings elsewhere in an increment (collectedBy, page/route references, e2e slugs) are PAGE SLUGS — a different namespace that stays kebab.

The test scaffolding is a hard dependency, not a convenience: pp-010 creates the test:plant-products script and contract.plant-products.test.js, pp-011 creates test:features:plant-products and the per-set Playwright project. Neither script exists in the frontend package.json today, so EVERY increment whose verification ladder runs them (or whose filesToTouch includes contract.plant-products.test.js) carries pp-010 and/or pp-011 in dependsOn — no increment may hedge with 'if the script has landed'.

RECIPE FIRST (R6, Sam 2026-08-01): pp-053 is the first increment in the programme and writes exactly ONE markdown file — src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md. It creates no directories, edits no dep-cruiser config, touches no package.json. Its value is that pp-056, pp-057, pp-006 and pp-007 stop being freehand platform work and become recipe-following, and its risk is that it is written against target seam shapes before running code exists. That risk is managed by the mandatory reconciliation step in each of those four increments, not by weakening the recipe.

CO-RESIDENCY IS THE ORGANISING CONSTRAINT (R3, Sam 2026-08-01): from pp-056 onward, 'does live-animals still work' and 'do BOTH sets work in the same process' are separate questions and both must be answered. co-residency.test.js (born in pp-006) and test:features:all (born in pp-011) are the two artefacts that answer the second one; once each exists it joins the standing ladder and is never dropped from a later increment's verification. Any increment that finds itself wanting a module-level single-slot singleton, a global URL constant, or an env var that picks a set has misread the ruling — pp-058's no-set-singletons.test.js exists to catch exactly that regression.

COPY IDEMPOTENCY BEFORE THE COPY BUTTON (R4, Sam 2026-08-01): pp-054 (backend header, unique partial index, return-the-existing-copy) and pp-055 (frontend adapters + records-port contract tests) both land in m0, and both are in pp-045's dependsOn. pp-045 is an UNPLANNED m5 stub under SD-12/R5, so it must not be planned here; when it is planned, its body must carry the four-rule rendering contract from the plant set charter (mint a randomUUID per RENDERED action, carry it in a hidden idempotencyKey input, re-render the SAME key on a recover path, never mint one per request). A Copy action arriving without pp-054 and pp-055 is a build-loop halt.

THE CROSS-REPO PAIR (R7, Sam 2026-08-01): pp-057 (frontend URL migration) and pp-059 (tests-repo URL migration) MUST land back to back with nothing between them. They CANNOT be atomic — different repos, different git histories — so between the two commits the workspace E2E suite is RED BY CONSTRUCTION: the moment live-animals registers under /live-animals, every URL in the tests repo points at a 404. That is expected and is not a regression. What IS a failure: landing pp-057 and then doing anything other than pp-059 next. Do not interleave, do not park it overnight, do not open an unrelated PR against either repo in between. If the loop has to be abandoned mid-pair, roll BOTH back with `git stash push -u` in each repo. pp-057 is itself ATOMIC and cannot be split — the moment live-animals is prefixed, every unmigrated call site is broken, so all of SIBLING-SET-PLAN §4.6 A-D lands in one increment.

THE TESTS-REPO LANE (R8, Sam 2026-08-01): repos/trade-imports-animals-tests is the THIRD repo in this programme and carries nine increments. pp-059 does the branch cut FIRST — that repo is on spike/EUDPA-288-model-retrofit today and CLAUDE.md rule 2 requires the shared name spike/trace-to-requirements across every affected repo — and no tests-repo change may land before that cut. Its increments are deliberately placed at the END of each milestone (pp-061 closes m1, pp-062 closes m2, pp-063 closes m3, pp-064/pp-065/pp-066 close m4, pp-067 closes the planned part of m5) so every spec asserts against pages that already exist. Its verification ladder is ITS OWN: typecheck, lint, format:check, test (which shells bin/assert-stack.sh and refuses to run without a stack), test:local, test:a11y, test:cross-browser, test:docker-compose. There is no vitest npm test, no test:features, no test:live-animals and no lint:arch in that repo, and no frontend script name may be copied into a tests-repo verification step. Run the workspace stack in DEV mode (run-stack.sh -d -b spike/trace-to-requirements) for all of it — a plain stack pulls Dockerhub :latest, which predates the mount and will fail every migrated assertion in a way that looks like the edits are wrong. Commit in that repo, on its branch, never from the workspace root.

gaps.gap: CLOSED BY PLAN, NOT BY EXTRACTION — no 'add a set' recipe existed in the repo, and round 1 treated SIBLING-SET-PLAN itself as the recipe with extraction deferred to an m4+ chore. Sam's ruling R6 (2026-08-01) reverses that: pp-053 AUTHORS src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md as the FIRST increment in the programme, before any sets/plant-products/ file exists, distilled from §8 G-A's ten steps plus §4.1 (set-context exports), §4.2 (the per-seam table), §4.3 (route shapes vs link builders and the mount table), §4.4.3-5 (the gateway call table, barrel and router registration), §1 (the m0 file list and required exports), §6.2 (the op->HTTP table including the R4 Idempotency-Key copy row), §7 (T-1..T-10 and the plant verification ladder), §5 P-4 (dep-cruiser edits) and §5 P-11 (the tripwire). pp-056, pp-057, pp-006 and pp-007 then FOLLOW the recipe verbatim, and each carries a MANDATORY doc-reconciliation step: re-read add-a-set.md at the end of the increment and correct any drift; a shape that could not be shipped as described means the recipe is wrong and is fixed there.

No depth-3 nested-collection recipe — add-a-collection's nested exemplar (animalIdentifiers) is only depth 2. Needs grouped-binding groups arrays of length 3, ...At path discipline, parent-index validation at TWO levels, and scope/wipe/completeness at depth. Unproven platform ground until pp-012 is green. Bites pp-012, pp-021, pp-025.

No 'create the hub from scratch' recipe — recipe §3.6 assumes an existing hub. Needs the controller GROUPS shape, numbered group captions in both locales, row title/hint copy contract, conditional:true hide semantics, review-spoke unlock wiring and hub axe/e2e baselines; transpose the live-animals hub feature file-for-file. Bites pp-007 (skeleton) and pp-029 (full build).

No records-adapter recipe — the recipes' persistence step ('edit the L2 notification-mapper') is inapplicable under FD-5. Needs the 11-op engine port surface, the op->HTTP table, stub/real parity including status-transition legality, mapper omission-assertion discipline (a field with no backend home gets an explicit omission test, never an invented property) and the documents sub-resource projection. Bites pp-008.

No entry-guard / opening-run authoring recipe — flow maintenance covers CHANGING flow data, not authoring entry-guard.js and run.js from nothing. Needs the policy contract: what entryGuardTarget may return, its allowed L2 reads, deep-link redirect policy, and which pages belong in RUN_STEPS. Bites pp-009.

No check-answers-from-scratch recipe — the recipes extend existing cards. Creating features/check-answers/ needs the view-model/cards directory contract, row()/changeAction() obligation-name resolution through dispatch, scope-driven row omission and the review -> declaration -> confirmation exit spine; transpose the live-animals feature. Bites pp-038.

No dashboard/lifecycle recipe — notifications-dashboard, delete-notification and the amend/copy actions have live exemplars (features/dashboard, features/notification-actions, features/delete-notification) but no recipe doc; plan by exemplar transposition citing concrete live-animals files. Bites pp-037 and pp-045.

No flow-only-key recipe — import-type and declaration ride FLOW_ONLY_KEYS/session, not the manifest (FD-8). Recipe fragments exist but no end-to-end script (key -> session store -> entry filter behaviour -> finalise-time inclusion); transpose the import-type-filter and declaration features. Bites pp-009, pp-017, pp-039.

No CSV-branch recipe anywhere — the branch-replacement pattern (same 12 obligations, alternate collection surface) has no live-animals analogue at all. An m5 problem, flagged now so nobody expects a recipe. Bites pp-042.

No 'add a set to the tests repo' recipe — repos/trade-imports-animals-tests has no equivalent of the frontend's docs/add-a-*.md, and its structure (tests/{a11y,e2e/{features,journeys,pages},cross-browser}, page-objects/{base,notification,admin,auth}, flows/, fixtures/, seeds/, adapters/, domain/, utils/, config/ and five Playwright configs) encodes a one-service assumption in several places at once. pp-060 establishes the convention by moving live-animals into a per-set tree and adding per-set Playwright projects, and every later tests-repo increment follows what pp-060 lands. Two config traps are recorded now rather than discovered later: utils/playwright/with-project-base-urls.ts holds a HARDCODED project-name to env-var map and throws for any project missing from projectBaseUrls, and playwright.e2e.config.ts and playwright.cross-browser.config.ts REPLACE the projects array wholesale rather than inheriting shared-config's, so editing shared-config alone leaves the workspace E2E and cross-browser lanes on the old shape. Bites pp-059, pp-060 and every tests-repo increment after them.

milestones.name: Backend schema, platform seams, symmetric mounts & set scaffold

increments.title: Author src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md — the add-a-set recipe, written BEFORE any plant-products file exists (R6 / G-A)
increments.recipe: This increment WRITES a recipe; it does not follow one. Its form is dictated by the existing recipe corpus — read src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-page.md and add-a-collection.md FIRST and match their voice, heading style and step shape exactly. Its content is distilled from SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §8 G-A (the 10 required steps), §4.1-§4.6 (the co-residency mechanism, the symmetric `'/' + setId` mount scheme and the enumerated live-animals URL migration), §10 (the tests-repo half), §1 (the m0 file list and exports), §6.2 (records port incl. the Idempotency-Key copy contract) and §7 (test scaffolding + verification ladder).

filesToTouch.what:
The add-a-set recipe. LOCATION IS LOAD-BEARING: it goes in the L1/platform docs dir alongside architecture.md, persistence.md and engine.md — NOT under sets/live-animals/docs/ (a set-level doc cannot own a cross-set procedure; SIBLING-SET-PLAN §8 G-A states this explicitly). FORM: match sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-page.md — an opening sentence saying when to use it and when not to, a 'Run every command from the frontend repo root' path-convention paragraph, a 'Read these files first' section listing concrete relative-link exemplars, then numbered '## N. <imperative step>' sections, each with the exact file/export/edit to make, then a verification section. GDS plain English, second person, no marketing. CONTENT — the ten steps of §8 G-A, restated for co-residency:

1. '## 1. Choose the set name and its mount prefix' — the co-residency contract stated plainly: BOTH gateways register in ONE Node process; every configure* seam is keyed by set id; a request resolves its set from the OWNING PLUGIN REALM, never by parsing the URL (FD-1/FD-14/FD-15). State the SYMMETRIC MOUNT rule (R7 — this REPLACES the reversed FD-16 wording; do not write 'the incumbent set keeps the root, a new set takes a prefix' anywhere in this file): **the mount prefix is NOT a choice — it is `'/' + setId`.** Every set mounts under its own prefix; NO set is ever registered at prefix '' and `registerSetMount` throws if one is passed. Give the reasoning in two lines: the set id is already the key for every other per-set fact (setKeyed, withSetContext, the plugin name, the cookie-name prefix, the sets/<setId>/ dir, the Nunjucks TEMPLATES root, the dep-cruiser regexes, the npm scripts, the Playwright project names), so deriving the mount from it means one fact per set and no mount table to drift; and with no set at '' a doubled prefix and a dropped prefix both fail visibly on the first request instead of producing the same correct-looking string for whichever set sat at the root. Then state the two consequences the author must not discover later: (a) FD-18 — `/` belongs to NO set; it is a server-wide 302 (never 301) to the default set's dashboard, declared with `server.route` in src/server/router.js behind a single DEFAULT_SET_BASE constant, OUTSIDE both gateways, so it never enters a set context and never appears in any set's allRoutes; (b) FD-19 — `/health`, `/signout`, the `/auth/*` OIDC routes and the static-asset route (`${assetPath}/{param*}`) are SERVER-WIDE and must NEVER sit inside a prefixed `server.register` call. Call out that signout is the live trap: it registers perfectly well at `/live-animals/signout` and nothing fails until a user tries to sign out, so it gets its own unprefixed register call and its own assertion. Include the mount table shape (set | prefix | dashboard | create | hub | page) with both sets filled in, and name the P-11 symmetry tripwire (src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js) here as well as in step 4 — it fails the build if a set is registered at '' or at anything other than '/' + setId. Cite §4.3 and §4.6.

2. '## 2. Create the L3 skeleton' — sets/<name>/obligations/index.js with `export const obligations = []`, the DERIVED groups formula copied verbatim from sets/live-animals/obligations/index.js (never hand-kept), and the `policy` export shape from P-1: `{ systemPopulated: [], enforcedAtContinue: [], maxEntriesFrom: {}, systemAnswerKeys: ['referenceNumber'] }`. State the rule that obligation names are camelCase, path-safe (no dots or brackets) or buildDispatch throws at boot, and carry NO display text.

3. '## 3. Create the L4 skeleton' — sets/<name>/journeys/linear/: config.js (TEMPLATES = '<name>/journeys/linear', LAYOUT = 'shared/layout.njk' unprefixed, and THREE SET-PREFIXED SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES — say explicitly that under co-residency these names are load-bearing, not cosmetic, because both sets' cookies live in the same browser at the same time); flow/flow.js (FLOW_ONLY_KEYS, sections, derived allFlowPages/sectionOfPage/answerSections); flow/task-rows.js (taskRows, rowStatus delegating to L2 bridge/status); flow/run.js (RUN_STEPS, nextRunTarget); flow/entry-guard.js (entryGuardTarget); features/index.js (dispatchPages, allRoutes); features/evaluation.js (featureEvaluationBindings = Object.freeze([])). Name the exact export names each file must have for configureJourneyFlow / buildDispatch to accept it.

4. '## 4. Write the L1 gateway' — the call table with the LOAD-BEARING ORDER: context → mount → config → assertions → dispatch → persistence → cookies → guard → priming → routes. Spell out: `registerSetMount(setId, '/' + setId)` — written that way, so the symmetry is in the code rather than in a convention someone has to remember; server.ext('onPreAuth', …enterSetContext(setId)…) as the FIRST thing in the register body; the whole body wrapped in `await withSetContext(setId, async () => { … })` because assertObligationPurity/assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage/buildDispatch read through currentSetId() outside any request; setId as the FIRST argument of configureObligationSet / configureFulfilmentRegistry / configureJourneyFlow / buildDispatch / configureRecords / configureSession; `registerJourneyCookie(server, { base: '/' + setId, cookieNames })` — again written with the derivation visible — so the three session cookies are path-scoped to the set's own subtree and one set's draft is invisible to another; which seams are OPTIONAL (configureCommodityReference — only the L2 live-animals mapper consumes it, so a set that owns its own records service never calls it and its slot is provably absent); when priming applies (countries.prime()/ports.prime() are live-animals-mode machinery and run on that gateway only — a fixture-backed set primes nothing). Point at the P-11 tripwire test (src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js) by name for BOTH of its rules, so the author meets them BEFORE writing the file: the setId-first seam rule AND the R7 symmetry rule (no set at '', every prefix exactly '/' + setId).

5. '## 5. Register the gateway' — add it to the routes.js barrel (`export { <name> } from './routes-<name>.js'`) and register it in src/server/router.js with its OWN `await server.register(<name>, { routes: { prefix: '/<name>' } })` call. Show the shape as ONE PREFIXED REGISTER CALL PER SET, one line each, plus the hoisted unprefixed `if (authEnabled) await server.register([signout])` and the `GET /` 302 route — i.e. show what the whole block looks like with two sets in it, not just the line being added. Say why each part is the way it is: `routes.prefix` applies to a WHOLE register call, so two sets can never share one; signout must not be in an array with a set gateway (FD-19) or it silently moves under that set's prefix; and the `/` redirect uses `server.route`, not a gateway, so it stays out of every set context (FD-18).

6. '## 6. Edit dependency-cruiser' — add the new gateway file to the routes-is-the-gateway pathNot allowlist and to the sets-not-l1 forbidden-target regex (sets must not import ANY routes-*.js). State the baseline rule loudly: do NOT regenerate .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json to absorb anything.

7. '## 7. Add the test scaffolding' — the set-scoped Vitest script (`test:<name>`), the per-set Playwright project (testDir at the set's features dir, same use block, specs navigating under the set's prefix), the cloned app-root suites (contract / routes / indexed / store-ops / one-load-per-request as *.<name>.test.js — each composes ONE set so the sole-set fallback means they need no context plumbing), the empty contract table with harness and zero cases, and A NEW CASE IN co-residency.test.js. Say that the parameterised fs-walk convention tests (copy-convention, copy-parity) loop over set roots in-file and need the new root added.

THEN A CROSS-REPO CLAUSE (R8 — the half that was missing from the plan entirely): **a set is not done when its in-repo tests pass.** The in-repo *.e2e.spec.js suites run against a self-hosted server on the records STUB; only repos/trade-imports-animals-tests runs the same journeys against the real workspace stack — real backend, real Mongo, real OIDC. So the recipe requires, in that repo and on the SAME branch name (CLAUDE.md rule 2): page objects under page-objects/<set-id>/ extending the set-aware NotificationPage with the set's base from page-objects/base/sets.ts; a flow under flows/<set-id>/; per-set specs under tests/{a11y,e2e/features,e2e/pages,e2e/journeys}/<set-id>/; a Playwright project frontend-<set-id>-chromium in utils/playwright/shared-config.ts, testMatch-scoped to that subtree and mapped to the SAME frontend base URL as every other set (the base URL is HOST-ONLY — a set-prefixed base URL breaks /signout, /health, assets and the OIDC callback and makes the other sets unreachable); and the project name added to every playwright.*.config.ts project list, to package.json's script flags and to the CI workflows, or CI silently stops running a whole set. Cite §10 (and §10.2 for the layer-by-layer parameterise-vs-clone ruling: one set-aware URL layer, two of everything above it).

8. '## 8. Stand up the set services' — mode switch (<NAME>_MODE, stub|real, default real); the records adapter against the set's own backend surface, presented as an engine-port-op → HTTP table (the 11 ops: create, load, list, has, replaceFulfilment, finalise, amend, cancelAmend, copy, softDelete, clear) INCLUDING THE Idempotency-Key CONTRACT FOR copy — a randomUUID() minted per RENDERED copy action, carried in a hidden input named idempotencyKey, sent as the Idempotency-Key request header by the real adapter, mirrored by a dedupe key in the stub, with records-port contract tests pinning 'one new draft per idempotency key' and 'copy idempotency scoped to the source reference'; reference-data fixtures. State the mapper omission discipline: a field with no backend home gets an explicit omission assertion, never an invented payload property.

9. '## 9. Build the minimum usable surfaces' — dashboard, hub (+ GROUPS), entry filter, entry-guard policy. Warn that the set's entry guard must derive its journey prefix from a FUNCTION (setBase()-derived), never a module-load const — name the live-animals JOURNEY_PREFIX bug class as the reason.

10. '## 10. Verify — the two-sided, co-residency ladder' — every set already in the tree AND the new set must serve correctly FROM ONE RUNNING PROCESS. The ladder: baseline `npm run test:<name>` before editing; then `npm run test:<name>`, `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `PORT=3050 npm run test:features:<name>`, `npm run test:features:all` (one server, both projects), `npm run test:e2e`, `npm run format`. co-residency.test.js must be green and must have gained a case for the new set — including that GET `/<name>` serves the new set, GET `/` still 302s to the default set, and `/signout`, `/health` and the static-asset route still resolve UNPREFIXED now that another prefixed register exists. THEN THE TESTS-REPO LEG (R8), which is part of the ladder and not an optional extra: on the same branch name, run the workspace E2E suite from repos/trade-imports-animals-tests against a co-resident stack — `npm run test:live-animals` and `npm run test:<name>` there, plus the full suite — and confirm both frontend Playwright projects are discovered by `playwright test --list`. State explicitly that the retired bar was 'the new set is green AND the default set is unchanged under its own env', and the current bar is 'EVERY set serves correctly from the same running process, proven in-repo by co-residency.test.js and test:features:all AND cross-repo by the tests-repo suite against the real stack'.

Close with a short '## What this recipe does not cover' section pointing at the remaining gaps by name (depth-3 nested collections, hub-from-scratch, check-answers-from-scratch, flow-only keys, CSV branch) so a future author does not assume coverage.

specs: NONE — documentation-only increment, no runnable spec. The recipe's correctness is proved downstream: every m0-b scaffold increment (pp-007 and its siblings) cites the add-a-set.md step it is executing, and any step that cannot be followed verbatim is a defect in THIS increment, fixed here rather than worked around in the scaffold.

increments.notes:
AMENDED FOR RULINGS R7 AND R8 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session). R7 — SYMMETRIC MOUNTS, FD-16 reversed: step 1's content is REWRITTEN. The sentence the round-2 recipe was to contain — 'the incumbent set keeps the root mount, every new set takes a prefix' — is deleted and must not reappear in any form. In its place: the mount prefix is not a choice, it is `'/' + setId`; no set owns `/`; `/` is a server-wide 302 to the default set (FD-18); and `/health`, `/signout`, `/auth/*` and the static-asset route are server-wide and must never sit inside a prefixed `server.register` call (FD-19, with signout named as the live trap because it registers happily at the wrong path). Step 4 now shows `registerSetMount(setId, '/' + setId)` and `registerJourneyCookie(server, { base: '/' + setId, cookieNames })` with the derivation visible in the code, and points at P-11's SYMMETRY tripwire as well as its setId-first one. Step 5 shows one prefixed register call per set PLUS the hoisted unprefixed signout register and the `/` redirect, as a whole block rather than a single added line. R8 — TESTS-REPO COVERAGE: step 7 gains a cross-repo clause (a set is not done until it has page objects, a flow, per-set specs and a Playwright project in repos/trade-imports-animals-tests, on the same branch name, with a HOST-ONLY base URL) and step 10's ladder gains the tests-repo leg. The file now cites §4.3, §4.6 and §10.

WHY THIS IS FIRST (Sam's ruling R6, 2026-08-01): round 1 said 'this plan IS the recipe; extracting docs/add-a-set.md afterwards is a recommended m4+ chore'. R6 reverses that. The recipe is authored BEFORE any sets/plant-products/ file exists and the m0 scaffold increments then FOLLOW it verbatim, exactly as the frontend-change skill follows add-a-field.md / add-a-page.md / add-a-collection.md. Writing it first is what closes gap G-A; extracting it afterwards would only document whatever happened to be built.

HEADLESS DECISION — dependsOn is [] (the orchestrator's explicit instruction: 'it is FIRST, before all m0 work'). This differs from SIBLING-SET-PLAN §9 step 7, which sequences the recipe AFTER P-9/P-10 so it can describe the seams 'as they actually are'. Recording the tension and the resolution: the recipe is authored against the TARGET seam shapes that §4.1/§4.2/§4.3 specify and that pp-056 (P-9) and pp-057 (P-10) implement. Because those sections specify the shapes down to function names and signatures, a doc written from them is not speculative — but it IS unverified against running code until the platform increments land. Mitigation, and it is mandatory: the implementor of pp-056, pp-057 and pp-006 must re-read add-a-set.md at the end of their increment and correct any drift between the doc and the seams they actually shipped. Mirror animals NotificationCopyMapperTest. Drive copyFrom(source) with fullyPopulatedNotification() in SUBMITTED state carrying a submittedBaseline, expireAt, declaration. The highest-value class; mirror animals NotificationServiceTest structure (@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class), @Mock PlantProductsNotificationRepository/PlantProductsAccompanyingDocumentRepository/PlantProductsNotificationMapper/PlantProductsNotificationCopyMapper/PlantProductsReferenceNumberGenerator/PlantProductsNotificationTtlConfig, service built by constructor with listPageSize e.g. 25; @Nested per operation). REPLACE: path/body referenceNumber mismatch -> PlantProductsBadRequestException; unknown ref -> upsert path creates (ReplaceResult.created true, server fields stamped); existing SUBMITTED or DELETED -> PlantProductsBadRequestException (writable = DRAFT/AMEND only); existing DRAFT -> content applied, updated re-stamped, created false. FIND: delegates to findByReferenceNumber. FINDALL: 1-based page converts to 0-based PageRequest with listPageSize and PlantProductsNotificationSort.toSort; status filter is exactly DRAFT/SUBMITTED/AMEND (DELETED hidden); referenceNumber param trims and exact-matches to a single-row page via findByReferenceNumberAndStatusIn, empty page when absent; response page number is 1-based. CHANGESTATUS — the five-row transition table, one test per row plus negatives: DRAFT->SUBMITTED captures submittedBaseline from current content; SUBMITTED->AMEND captures submittedBaseline; AMEND->SUBMITTED with discardChanges null/false re-captures the baseline from amended content; AMEND->SUBMITTED with discardChanges true restores content via snapshot applyTo and keeps the old baseline; DRAFT/SUBMITTED/AMEND->DELETED soft-deletes; DELETED->DELETED is idempotent (200-equivalent, no exception); every transition not in the table -> PlantProductsBadRequestException (parameterise the illegal from/to pairs); discardChanges=true on any transition other than AMEND->SUBMITTED -> PlantProductsBadRequestException; unknown ref -> PlantProductsNotFoundException. COPY: delegates to copyMapper.copyFrom, re-mints a fresh reference (with the same 3-retry DuplicateKeyException loop), returns a new DRAFT; source in DRAFT or DELETED -> PlantProductsBadRequestException (copyable = SUBMITTED/AMEND); unknown ref -> PlantProductsNotFoundException; verify NO writes to the accompanying-document repository (copies start documentless, D-19). increments.title: Backend: copy idempotency — Idempotency-Key on POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies (R4)
increments.recipe: No frontend recipe applies. The script is a TRANSPOSITION of the live-animals implementation, which is the canonical reference per Sam's ruling R4 — read all five live-animals files named in notes before writing anything, and mirror their structure call-for-call. NOTE THE TRANSPOSITION: live-animals implements idempotency on the FULFILMENT resource (POST /fulfilments/{id}/copy); plant-products puts /copies on the NOTIFICATION resource (POST /plant-products/notifications/{reference-number}/copies). Transpose the pattern, not the code — the aggregate, the id field name, the exception types and the not-found/bad-request classes all differ.

filesToTouch.what: Add the idempotency field and its unique partial index. TODAY (verified live) the class carries a SINGLE @CompoundIndex(name = "org_status_dashboard", def = "{'ownership.assignedOrganisationId': 1, 'status': 1}") directly on the type. Two indexes cannot both sit as bare @CompoundIndex annotations, so wrap them in @CompoundIndexes({ … }) exactly as animals/fulfilment/Fulfilment.java:15-27 does: keep org_status_dashboard verbatim and add @CompoundIndex(name = "copy_idempotency_key", def = "{'copyIdempotencyKey': 1}", unique = true, partialFilter = "{'copyIdempotencyKey': {'$type': 'string'}}") — name, def and partialFilter byte-identical to the live-animals index apart from nothing (the field name is the same). The partial filter is load-bearing: without it every notification with a null copyIdempotencyKey (i.e. every notification that is not a copy) would collide on the unique index. Add the field alongside the existing id/submittedBaseline/expireAt members: `private String copyIdempotencyKey;` — NO @JsonIgnore (mirrors Fulfilment.java:47 exactly; see the deviation note in notes). Add the org.springframework.data.mongodb.core.index.CompoundIndexes import. The field goes on PlantProductsNotification, NOT on PlantProductsNotificationBase — Base is shared with PlantProductsNotificationContentSnapshot and the DTO, and an idempotency key is neither content nor a snapshotable value.

Add one derived query beside the existing findByReferenceNumber: `Optional<PlantProductsNotification> findByCopyIdempotencyKey(String copyIdempotencyKey);` — exact transposition of animals/fulfilment/FulfilmentRepository.java:10. No other change; Optional is already imported.

Change `public PlantProductsNotification copy(String referenceNumber)` (today at line 144, @Transactional) to `public PlantProductsNotification copy(String referenceNumber, String idempotencyKey)` and give it the four-part live-animals shape from FulfilmentService.copy (lines 108-155):
(1) BLANK GUARD FIRST, before any repository read: `if (idempotencyKey == null || idempotencyKey.isBlank()) throw new PlantProductsBadRequestException("Idempotency-Key must not be blank");` — same message string as live-animals, plant exception type.
(2) LOOKUP-AND-RETURN-EXISTING: a private `findCopy(String idempotencyKey)` helper returning `notificationRepository.findByCopyIdempotencyKey(idempotencyKey).orElse(null)`; if non-null, log at info ('Returning existing plant-products notification copy {} for idempotency key') and RETURN IT UNCHANGED — no new document, no status change, no re-stamped timestamps. This is the whole point: a repeated key is answered with the copy already made.
(3) The existing source lookup and copyable guard stay exactly as they are (findByReferenceNumber → PlantProductsNotFoundException; status must be SUBMITTED or AMEND else PlantProductsBadRequestException("Cannot copy notification with status: " + status)). They run AFTER the idempotency short-circuit, so a repeat of a key whose source has since been deleted still returns the copy.
(4) The copy build gains `copy.setCopyIdempotencyKey(idempotencyKey);` alongside the existing setChedType/setStatus(DRAFT)/setCreated/setUpdated/stampExpiry, and persists through a NEW private `saveCopyWithMintedReference(PlantProductsNotification copy, String idempotencyKey)` rather than the shared saveWithMintedReference. Why a separate method: saveWithMintedReference's MAX_REF_RETRIES loop treats every DuplicateKeyException as a reference-number collision and retries, which is now wrong — the exception can also come from the copy_idempotency_key unique index when two concurrent requests carry the same key. The new method mirrors FulfilmentService.copy's loop: on DuplicateKeyException, FIRST re-check findCopy(idempotencyKey) and, if a copy now exists, log ('Returning concurrently-created plant-products notification copy {}') and return it; only if that is still null treat the exception as a reference collision, log the retry warning and go round again; after MAX_REF_RETRIES throw the existing IllegalStateException message. Leave saveWithMintedReference untouched for create/replace — this increment must not change the plain create path.
Method stays @Transactional.

Make the header a REQUIRED request header on the copies endpoint. Add `public static final String IDEMPOTENCY_KEY = "Idempotency-Key";` as the first member of the class (transposition of FulfilmentController.java:37 — a public constant so the tests and any future client bind to the name rather than a string literal). Add the org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestHeader import. On the existing @PostMapping("/{reference-number}/copies") method (today at lines 156-171), add a second parameter `@RequestHeader(IDEMPOTENCY_KEY) String idempotencyKey` — note the DEFAULT required=true is deliberate and load-bearing: an absent header must be a 400, not a copy with a null key. Pass it through: `notificationService.copy(referenceNumber, idempotencyKey)`. Update the OpenAPI annotations to match live-animals' wording: the @Operation description gains 'Repeating the request with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same copy with the same Location.' and the existing 400 @ApiResponse description becomes 'Source notification is not in a copyable state or the Idempotency-Key header is blank'. Response body and Location header are unchanged — a repeat returns 201 with the SAME body and the SAME Location, which is what makes the browser's double-submit harmless.

CONDITIONAL edit — read the file first. A missing required @RequestHeader raises Spring's MissingRequestHeaderException (a ServletRequestBindingException), which Spring MVC's default handling maps to 400. If this handler has a catch-all @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) that would swallow it into a 500, add an explicit @ExceptionHandler(MissingRequestHeaderException.class) returning 400 with the same ProblemDetail/body shape the handler already uses for PlantProductsBadRequestException. If the default 400 already survives (verify by running the new controller test, not by reading), make NO edit to this file and delete it from the diff. Do not guess — the controller test in this increment is what decides.

Add the copy-idempotency unit cases to the existing service test (create the class in the house style if pp-003 has not landed it yet — same package as the production class, Mockito @Mock repositories/mappers/generator, @InjectMocks service, matching the sibling animals FulfilmentServiceTest idiom). Cases, one behaviour each: (1) ROUND-TRIP — a fresh key with a SUBMITTED source inserts exactly one document whose copyIdempotencyKey equals the supplied key, status DRAFT, a newly minted reference, content fields carried over; (2) NEGATIVE, repeat key — findByCopyIdempotencyKey returns an existing copy, so the service returns THAT document and `verify(notificationRepository, never()).insert(any())` (this is the one place a call-verification is right: 'did not write' is the behaviour under test, not an implementation detail); (3) NEGATIVE, blank key — null, "" and "   " each throw PlantProductsBadRequestException with message 'Idempotency-Key must not be blank', and no repository read of the source happens; (4) CONCURRENCY — insert throws DuplicateKeyException on the first attempt, the second findByCopyIdempotencyKey returns a document, and the service returns it without retrying the mint; (5) REFERENCE COLLISION still works — insert throws DuplicateKeyException, findByCopyIdempotencyKey stays empty, the service mints again and succeeds on attempt 2 (proves the new recovery path did not break collision retry). Do NOT add a case per status enum value — one copyable-status positive and one non-copyable-status negative only (house rule: tests do not scale with enum constants).

Add the header-binding cases to the existing controller test (create in house style if absent — @WebMvcTest or standalone MockMvc as the sibling animals controller test does; match whichever the repo already uses). Cases: (1) POST …/copies WITH an Idempotency-Key header → the service is called with (referenceNumber, headerValue) and the response is 201 with the Location header; (2) POST …/copies WITHOUT the header → 400 and the service is NEVER called (this is the case that proves required=true and settles whether PlantProductsExceptionHandler needs the MissingRequestHeaderException mapping — if this test yields 500, make that handler edit); (3) POST …/copies with a blank header value → reaches the service and surfaces its PlantProductsBadRequestException as 400 (blank is a service-level guard, not a binding-level one — same split as live-animals).

Add the end-to-end idempotency proof to the IT pp-004 creates (if pp-004 has not landed, this increment creates the file with only these cases and pp-004 merges its own into the same class — the two increments must not both claim the same test method names). All HTTP via webClient("NoAuth") from IntegrationBase. Cases: (1) THE HEADLINE — create a notification, transition it to SUBMITTED, then POST …/copies TWICE with the SAME Idempotency-Key header; assert both responses are 201, both carry the SAME referenceNumber and the SAME Location, and that PlantProductsNotificationRepository.findAllByStatusIn([DRAFT], …) shows exactly ONE draft copy of that source — one new draft per idempotency key, proved against a real Mongo, not a mock; (2) two DIFFERENT keys against the same source produce TWO distinct drafts with distinct reference numbers (proves the dedupe is keyed, not a blanket one-copy-per-source rule); (3) SCOPING — the same key replayed is answered with the copy already made even when a second, different source notification is named in the path (records the live-animals semantic: the key alone identifies the copy; add this as an explicit assertion so the behaviour is pinned rather than accidental, and see openQuestions); (4) missing Idempotency-Key header → 400 and no draft created; blank header → 400 and no draft created; (5) INDEX PROOF — insert two PlantProductsNotification documents directly through the repository with the same non-null copyIdempotencyKey and assert DuplicateKeyException, then insert two with NULL copyIdempotencyKey and assert both succeed (this is the assertion that proves the unique PARTIAL index is actually live in Mongo; auto-index-creation is true in application.yml and application-integration-test.yml — verified — so a failure here means the annotation is wrong, not the config).

VERIFIED LIVE THIS SESSION (do not re-derive): PlantProductsNotificationController is @RequestMapping("/plant-products/notifications"), @Validated, and its copies method is at lines 156-171 taking only the reference-number path variable; PlantProductsNotificationService.copy is at line 144 with MAX_REF_RETRIES = 3, CHED_TYPE = "CHEDPP", saveWithMintedReference at line 262; PlantProductsNotification has exactly one @CompoundIndex today plus @JsonIgnore submittedBaseline and @JsonIgnore @Indexed expireAt; PlantProductsNotificationCopyMapper.copyFrom copies content + ownership and deliberately carries neither declaration nor documents (D-19); spring.data.mongodb.auto-index-creation is true in both application.yml and application-integration-test.yml, so the annotation alone creates the index.

Idempotency scope: live-animals keys the dedupe on the KEY ALONE (findByCopyIdempotencyKey), so a replayed key returns the same copy even if a different source reference is in the path — whereas the frontend contract test named in R4 is worded 'copy idempotency scoped to the source reference'. The script is SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §4.1 (the set-context module, quoted there in full) and §4.2 rows 1-8 (the per-seam table, one row per file with its today/after shape), plus §5 P-9 for the acceptance bar. filesToTouch.what: The one new L2 module. It is set-AGNOSTIC — it stores set ids and prefixes handed to it and imports nothing under sets/ — so dependency-cruiser needs no new rule for it. Implement exactly the module quoted at SIBLING-SET-PLAN §4.1: an AsyncLocalStorage from node:async_hooks; a module-level `mounts = new Map()` of setId → prefix, which under R7 is ALWAYS `'/' + setId` — NO set is ever registered at ''; `registerSetMount(setId, prefix)` which REJECTS an absent, empty or non-slash-leading prefix by throwing (`if (!prefix?.startsWith('/')) throw new Error(`Set "${setId}" needs a mount prefix`)`) — there is no `prefix = ''` default and no root-mount special case, because R7 reversed FD-16 and made every mount symmetric; `mountedSetIds()`; a private `soleSetId()` returning the only key when mounts.size === 1 and undefined otherwise; `currentSetId()` returning `storage.getStore()?.setId ?? soleSetId()` and THROWING new Error('No set context — no active set and more than one mounted') when neither yields an id; `currentSetBase()` = `mounts.get(currentSetId()) ?? ''` — carry a comment on that line saying the `?? ''` is a DEFENSIVE DEFAULT ONLY: no registered set has an empty prefix (registerSetMount rejects one, and pp-058's P-11 tripwire asserts at boot that every registered prefix equals `'/' + setId`), so a `''` here means a set id with no mount, not a root-mounted set; `withSetContext(setId, fn)` = storage.run({ setId }, fn) for BOOT time; `enterSetContext(setId)` = storage.enterWith({ setId }) for REQUEST time; and `setKeyed(label)` returning `{ configure(setId, value), current(), has(setId) }` over a per-seam Map, where current() resolves currentSetId() and throws `${label} not configured for set "${setId}"` when the slot is absent. THE SOLE-SET FALLBACK IN currentSetId() IS THE LOAD-BEARING DESIGN DECISION (FD-17): it is what lets every existing unit test, contract.test.js, routes.test.js, indexed.test.js, store-ops.test.js and each set's own suites keep working unchanged, because they each compose exactly ONE set; and it is what makes a missing context a loud failure in the co-resident server where it actually matters. Do not weaken it to a silent default and do not extend it to pick a 'first' set when several are mounted.

Unit-pin the module's own contract before any seam uses it: registerSetMount then currentSetBase returns the registered prefix; NEGATIVE CASE (R7, load-bearing) — `registerSetMount('x', '')` THROWS, and so do `registerSetMount('x')` and `registerSetMount('x', 'x')` (no leading slash); the message names the set id. This is the unit-level half of the symmetry rule pp-058 enforces at boot, and it is what stops a later increment quietly reinstating the root mount FD-16 reversed; with ONE mount and no active context, currentSetId returns that sole set (the FD-17 fallback); with TWO mounts and no active context, currentSetId THROWS; withSetContext(setId, fn) resolves currentSetId inside fn and restores the previous state after; enterSetContext persists across an await inside the same async context; setKeyed holds two different values for two different setIds simultaneously and current() throws a message naming the label and the set when the slot is unconfigured. Add ONE interleaving test here as well as in co-residency.test.js later: two async functions entered under different set ids, the first awaiting a deferred promise, each still reading its own value after resuming — this is the ALS risk §4.1 says must be retired, not assumed, and pinning it at the module level makes a failure diagnosable.

increments.notes:
RULING R7 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session): SYMMETRIC MOUNTS — FD-16 IS REVERSED. Sam does not accept live-animals keeping the root while only plant-products is prefixed: 'this stuff is still in development, refactoring live-animals is fine — have them match up; changing URLs if required, just make sure to update the -tests repo as well.' BOTH sets mount under `/<setId>`. live-animals' URLs MOVE to /live-animals. That is the whole character of this increment: it is a URL MIGRATION, not a no-op platform change.

THE ACCEPTANCE BAR THAT WAS DELETED. The round-2 version of this increment said: 'with live-animals still the only registered set, EVERY existing URL assertion in the repo passes UNEDITED — that is the proof the root mount is genuinely a no-op.' That bar is now WRONG in both directions: zero spec edits would mean the mount did nothing, and an assertion that survives the migration unchanged is an assertion that never tested the prefix. The replacement is the 8-point bar above: an explicit enumerated migration proven by UPDATED, FRONT-ANCHORED assertions.

WHY SYMMETRY IS SAFER, NOT JUST TIDIER (the trap R7 removes). Under the asymmetric plan live-animals sat at prefix '', so a DOUBLED prefix (setBase() used where a route shape was wanted) and a DROPPED prefix (a route shape used where a link was wanted) produced the SAME correct-looking string for live-animals — `'' + '/notifications'` is `/notifications` either way. The bug could only ever surface on the plant side, in code the live-animals suite never exercises, and the 'every live-animals assertion passes unedited' bar would have actively certified it as fine. With neither set at '', both mistakes fail visibly for BOTH sets on the first request. Symmetry costs one enumerated migration once; asymmetry costs a permanent special case in shared/paths.js, registerSetMount and add-a-set.md, plus a hidden bug class.

WHY THE ROUTE-SHAPE / LINK SPLIT IS UNAVOIDABLE (FD-4): shared/kit.js:120-133 calls pageRoutePath(slug) at MODULE LOAD when it builds pageRoutes, long before any configure* seam runs and with no request in flight. Route paths therefore CANNOT come from request context. Hapi's plugin `routes.prefix` supplies the mount instead, so route-shape builders stay prefix-free; only the link builders, which run per request, resolve setBase().

THIS INCREMENT IS ATOMIC AND CANNOT BE SPLIT. The moment live-animals is registered under a prefix, every unmigrated call site is broken. Splitting it (platform first, specs later) leaves the repo red between increments, which the build loop treats as a failure. All of §4.6 A-D lands here, in one commit if possible.

THE MOUNT TABLE this increment makes real (§4.3): live-animals prefix '/live-animals' → dashboard /live-animals, create /live-animals/notifications, hub /live-animals/notifications/{journeyId}, page /live-animals/notifications/{journeyId}/{slug}. plant-products (pp-007) takes the identical shapes under /plant-products. Route shapes are declared prefix-free and byte-identical between the sets; Hapi supplies the mount. A route registered as '/' under prefix '/live-animals' is served at '/live-animals' with NO trailing slash.

WHAT SERVES `/` (FD-18): a server-wide 302 redirect to /live-animals, declared with server.route in router.js next to health and signout, NEVER inside a gateway (so it never enters a set context and never appears in either set's allRoutes). Chosen over a set-picker page and over a 404 because OIDC is the binding constraint: auth/controller.js falls back to '/' in five places and getSafeRedirect only permits relative paths, so a 404 at '/' would break sign-in for anyone arriving without a stored redirect. A picker page needs new copy in two locales, a11y baselines and a design decision nobody has made — gold-plating for a two-set service still in development; it is the recorded upgrade path for when a third set lands. 302 not 301 because a 301 is cached indefinitely by browsers. NO legacy /notifications/* compatibility shim: there are no external bookmarks to honour at this stage, and a shim would have to guess which set a bare journey id belongs to.

FD-19 — THE DEFECT THIS INCREMENT WOULD INTRODUCE IF UNPLANNED: today router.js:20-24 pushes signout into the SAME register array as liveAnimals. Adding `{ routes: { prefix: '/live-animals' } }` to that call silently moves /signout to /live-animals/signout. It registers fine; nothing fails; the OIDC sign-out leg just breaks in the browser. Hoist it into its own unprefixed register and PIN it (router suite case (b)). The same check was applied and cleared for /health (own register, line 16) and the static-asset route (own register, line 29).

VERIFIED LIVE: shared/paths.js is 15 lines with `export const BASE = ''` at line 1 and dashboardPath() returning a bare '/' at line 10; engine/journey.js imports BASE at line 2 and freezes cookieOptions at lines 14-23 with `path: BASE || '/'`; router.js:7,16,20-24,29; entry-guard.js:1,13,16,18; dashboard/controller.js:114,126.

SCOPE FENCES: no gateway split, no barrel, no onPreAuth, no plant file — all pp-006/pp-007. No obligation-source policy work — pp-005 (which edits a DIFFERENT part of entry-guard.js; see its notes for the collision and the ordering). This increment registers only live-animals; the plant-products entry in shared/paths.test.js is a mount-table entry, never a real plugin.

CROSS-REPO PAIRING (§9 constraint 16): pp-057 and pp-059 are a PAIR across two repos on the SAME branch name `spike/trace-to-requirements` (CLAUDE.md rule 2). Between them the workspace E2E suite is red BY CONSTRUCTION. Do not sequence other work between them, and do not attempt to fix the tests repo from here — pp-059 owns the branch cut there (that repo is currently on spike/EUDPA-288-model-retrofit) and the §10.4 migration.

DOC RECONCILIATION (obligation carried from pp-053): re-read src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md at the end and correct any drift between what it says about mount prefixes, setBase(), the '/' redirect, the signout hoist and registerJourneyCookie and what actually shipped.

Commit in THIS repo, on ITS branch. Do not commit tests-repo changes from the workspace root.

SEQUENCING — THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING NOTE. pp-057 (frontend URL migration) and pp-059 (this) MUST land together, back to back, with nothing between them. They CANNOT be atomic — different repos, different git histories — so between the two commits the workspace E2E suite is RED BY CONSTRUCTION: the moment live-animals is registered under `/live-animals`, every URL in this repo points at a 404. That is expected, it is not a regression, and it is not a reason to stop. What IS a reason to stop: landing pp-057 and then doing anything other than pp-059 next. Do not interleave, do not park it overnight, do not open an unrelated PR against either repo in between. If the loop has to be abandoned mid-pair, roll BOTH back (`git stash push -u` in each repo — never `reset --hard` + `clean -fd`).

WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL (R7, Sam, 2026-08-01): FD-16 is reversed. Both sets mount under their own prefix — `/live-animals` and `/plant-products` — and no set owns `/`. Sam's reasoning: the service is still in development, so refactoring live-animals is fine; have the two sets match up, change URLs if that is what symmetry requires, and update the -tests repo as well. Symmetry is not merely tidiness here: with live-animals at prefix `''`, a doubled prefix and a dropped prefix produce the SAME correct-looking string for live-animals, so that whole bug class only ever surfaces on the plant side, in code this suite never runs. With both sets prefixed, both mistakes fail visibly on the first request.

WHY THE URL LAYER IS CHEAP AND THE SPECS ARE NOT: §10.2's ruling is one set-aware URL layer, two of everything above it. `base-page.ts` is genuinely centralised (verified live: two `page.goto` entry points, three URL builders), so six edits there carry most of the repo. The expensive half is judgement, not mechanics — the front-anchoring sweep. A regex like `/\/notifications\/abc$/` passes before AND after the migration; leaving it is leaving a spec that would also pass if someone silently dropped the prefix again.

WHAT `/` DOES NOW (FD-18): a server-wide 302 to `/live-animals`, declared in `src/server/router.js` outside both gateways so it never enters a set context. 302 not 301 — a 301 is cached by browsers indefinitely and would be painful to unpick when a set-picker page eventually replaces it. There is NO legacy `/notifications/*` compatibility shim: no external bookmarks to honour at this stage, and a shim would have to guess which set a bare journey id belongs to. So a stale deep link 404s, by design.

STACK: run the workspace stack in dev mode against this branch (`run-stack.sh -d -b spike/trace-to-requirements`) so you are testing the frontend source that pp-057 just changed, not a Dockerhub `:latest` image that predates the mount. `npm run test` shells `bin/assert-stack.sh` first and will refuse to run without a stack; a plain (non-`-d`) stack pulls `:latest` and will fail every migrated assertion in a way that looks like your edits are wrong.

OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately: the per-set directory move (`page-objects/notification/` → `page-objects/live-animals/`), the per-set Playwright projects and any plant-products file. All pp-060 onwards. This increment changes URLs and nothing else, so that if the suite goes red the cause is unambiguous.
