increments.title: P-11: setId-first + symmetric-mount convention tripwire — no-set-singletons.test.js guards against re-singletoning a seam and against reinstating a root mount
increments.recipe: No recipe covers convention tests. The script is SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §5 P-11 (BOTH assertions — the setId-first rule and the R7 symmetry rule), §4.3 (the `prefix = '/' + setId` scheme) and §7 T-10; the FORM is the existing fs-walk convention test src/server/app/copy-convention.test.js — read it first and mirror its structure (node:fs readdirSync + node:url fileURLToPath + a describe with a 'Should find the …' guard case before the real assertions).

filesToTouch.what:
A cheap, mechanical tripwire so a future increment cannot quietly reintroduce a single-slot seam after pp-056 removed them all.

WALK: the L2 directories model/, bridge/, flow/, engine/ and services/ under src/server/app, recursively, collecting every .js file that is not a .test.js. Use the same idiom as copy-convention.test.js — `readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })` (or the plain recursive form plus a path join, whichever the repo's Node version and existing file use) and `fileURLToPath(new URL('./model', import.meta.url))` for the roots, so the test is location-independent.

RULE: read each file's source and find every exported function whose name starts with `configure`. For each one, assert its FIRST PARAMETER IS NAMED `setId`. Match the declaration forms the codebase actually uses — `export const configureX = (setId, …) =>` and `export function configureX(setId, …)` — with a regex over the source text; this is a convention test, not a compiler, and a source-text match is both sufficient and the cheapest thing that cannot rot. If a configure* export is found whose first parameter is not setId, FAIL with a message naming the file, the export and the parameter it found, so the failure is self-explaining without opening the test.

GUARD CASE FIRST (copy-convention.test.js precedent): an `it('Should find the configure seams')` asserting the walk discovered at least the seven known seams by name — configureObligationSet, configureFulfilmentRegistry, configureJourneyFlow, configureRecords, configureSession, configureCommodityReference (and buildDispatch, see below). Without that guard, a broken walk that finds NOTHING passes vacuously, which is the classic way a convention test dies silently.

buildDispatch: it is a seam with the same setId-first contract but does not match the configure* name pattern. Include it as an explicit named check in the same file rather than widening the regex (widening would sweep in every build* helper in the codebase and produce false positives).

ALLOW-LIST: an empty array, exported as a named const at the top of the file with a comment saying it is empty BY DESIGN and that adding an entry means a seam has been exempted from co-residency — which is a decision, not a fix.

SECOND ASSERTION — THE R7 SYMMETRY TRIPWIRE (added by ruling R7; the file now guards TWO invariants). In the same file, a second describe: register EVERY gateway the app exports — import them from `src/server/app/routes.js` and register them against a booted Hapi server exactly as router.js does (at THIS increment routes.js is still the un-split live-animals gateway, so that is one gateway; drive the test off the module's exports rather than a hardcoded list, so pp-006's barrel and pp-007's `plantProducts` export are covered automatically with NO edit to this file) — and then assert, over `mountedSetIds()` and the registry: (a) NO set is mounted at prefix '' (and, defensively, `registerSetMount(id, '')` throws); (b) every registered prefix matches `/^\/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/` — one lowercase segment, no nesting, no trailing slash; (c) every registered prefix is EXACTLY `'/' + setId` for its own set id, which is the whole scheme in one line and the only assertion that cannot drift. Fail with a message naming the set id and the offending prefix. Guard case first, same rule as the seam walk: assert the registry discovered AT LEAST ONE mount, so a boot that silently registered nothing cannot pass vacuously.

WHY THIS SECOND ASSERTION EXISTS: R7 reversed FD-16's asymmetric scheme (live-animals at the root, plant-products prefixed). Without a mechanical guard, a later increment can quietly reinstate it — and the asymmetry is not merely untidy, it HIDES a bug class: with a set at '', a doubled prefix and a dropped prefix produce the same correct-looking string for that set, so the fault only ever surfaces on the other set, in code that set's suite never runs. Keeping every set off '' is what keeps both mistakes visible on the first request.

NO dependency-cruiser rule accompanies this: the constraint is about a function's parameter shape, which dep-cruiser cannot express. That is exactly why a convention test is the right instrument here.

TWO steps now cite this tripwire, not one (R7). Step 4 of the recipe (write the L1 gateway) already points at it per pp-053: verify it does, and correct it to name the file exactly as shipped — `src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js` — and to state the seam rule in one sentence: every configure* seam takes setId as its first parameter, the allow-list is empty by design, and a new seam that cannot take setId is a co-residency decision to raise, not a test to exempt. STEP 1 (choose the set id) must ALSO cite it, for the symmetry rule: the mount prefix is not a choice, it is `'/' + setId`; no set owns `/`; and this test fails the build if a set is registered at '' or at anything other than `'/' + setId`. Naming it in step 1 is what stops the next author from 'just taking the root because ours is the main journey'. If pp-053's text already says both things correctly, make no edit and drop the file from the diff.

specs: src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js — IS the deliverable; it is a convention test, not a test of new behaviour.
acceptanceCriteria: src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js walks model/, bridge/, flow/, engine/ and services/ under src/server/app and fails any non-test .js file that exports a configure* function whose first parameter is not named setId.
It additionally pins buildDispatch's setId-first contract by name, without widening the configure* regex to build*.
It is GREEN on pp-056's output with an EMPTY allow-list — no seam needs an exemption.

It is RED if setId is dropped from any seam: prove this during the increment by temporarily removing setId from one seam's signature, watching the test fail with a message naming that file and export, then reverting. Record in the commit message that the red was observed — a tripwire never seen red is a tripwire that may not work.

R7 SYMMETRY ASSERTION: with every gateway routes.js exports registered, no set is mounted at prefix '', every registered prefix matches /^\/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/, and every registered prefix equals '/' + its own setId. The test is driven off routes.js's exports, so pp-006's barrel and pp-007's plantProducts gateway are covered with no edit to this file.

It is RED if any set is registered at '' or at a prefix that is not '/' + setId: prove this too, by temporarily changing one registerSetMount call, watching the named failure, and reverting. Both reds are recorded in the commit message. This is the guard that stops a later increment quietly reinstating the asymmetry FD-16 reversed — and with it the doubled/dropped-prefix bug class that an empty prefix hides.

A vacuous pass is impossible on EITHER assertion: one guard case asserts the walk discovered the seven known seams by name, and a second asserts the mount registry discovered at least one mount, so a broken walk or a boot that registered nothing fails loudly instead of finding nothing and going green.
The failure message names the file, the export and the offending parameter name.

It follows the fs-walk idiom of copy-convention.test.js (node:fs readdirSync, fileURLToPath-based roots, a 'Should find …' guard case first) so it reads as idiomatic to this codebase rather than as a foreign gadget.

docs/add-a-set.md steps 1 AND 4 name this file and state their respective rules (step 1 the symmetric-mount rule, step 4 the setId-first rule), so the next set's author meets both before writing their gateway.
No dependency-cruiser rule is added and .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json is not regenerated.
npm test, npm run test:live-animals and npm run lint are green; no existing suite's test count drops; no production file is edited by this increment.

increments.notes:
AMENDED FOR RULING R7 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session). The file now guards TWO invariants, not one: the setId-first seam rule (R3) and the SYMMETRIC MOUNT rule (R7 — every set at `'/' + setId`, no set at ''). SIZE stays S: it is one more describe in the same file, and both assertions are cheap source-level/registry-level checks. SEQUENCING NOTE: dependsOn grows to pp-057, because the symmetry assertion needs the mounts to actually be `'/' + setId` — pp-056 declares the mount, pp-057 makes it real; running this tripwire before pp-057 would assert a scheme the app is not yet serving.

RULING R3 (Sam, 2026-08-01) makes co-residency a standing property of the platform, not a one-off migration. pp-056 keyed every seam by set; this increment stops the keying from decaying. It is deliberately the cheapest thing that works — a source-text convention test — because an expensive guard gets deleted the first time it is inconvenient.

WHY A CONVENTION TEST AND NOT A LINT/ARCH RULE: dependency-cruiser reasons about MODULE GRAPHS. The constraint here is about a FUNCTION'S PARAMETER SHAPE, which dep-cruiser cannot express at all. ESLint could in principle, via a custom rule, but a custom rule is a package, a config entry and a maintenance surface; the fs-walk convention test is a pattern this codebase ALREADY uses (copy-convention.test.js, copy-parity.test.js), so it is idiomatic and needs no new tooling.

SEQUENCING: it lands immediately after pp-056 and BEFORE the gateway split (pp-006), so that nothing from the gateway work onwards can re-singleton a seam. SIBLING-SET-PLAN §9 phase m0-a puts it at step 4, after P-10 (pp-057) and before P-4/P-3 — dependsOn is pp-056 AND pp-057: the seam rule needs the keyed seams to be green against, and the R7 symmetry rule needs the mounts to be real, which is pp-057's doing.

EXEMPLAR (read first): src/server/app/copy-convention.test.js — verified live this session; it imports readdirSync from node:fs, path from node:path and fileURLToPath from node:url, builds its root with `fileURLToPath(new URL('./sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features', import.meta.url))`, filters directory entries, uses `readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` for the deep walk, and opens its describe with an `it('Should find the feature folders')` guard asserting the walk found something. Mirror all four of those choices.

THE SEVEN SEAMS the guard case must name (from SIBLING-SET-PLAN §4.2 rows 1-7): configureObligationSet (model/obligations/manifest.js), configureFulfilmentRegistry (bridge/fulfilment-registry.js), configureJourneyFlow (flow/journey-flow.js), buildDispatch (flow/dispatch.js — named separately, see filesToTouch), configureRecords (engine/persistence/records.js), configureSession (engine/persistence/session.js), configureCommodityReference (services/persistence/records/notification-mapper/commodity-reference.js).

OBSERVE THE RED. The single most common failure mode for a tripwire is that it never actually fires. The acceptance criteria require temporarily breaking one seam's signature, seeing the named failure, and reverting — do it, and say so in the commit message.

SCOPE FENCE: this increment adds ONE test file (plus at most a one-paragraph doc correction). It edits no production file. If the walk finds a genuine violation in existing code, that is pp-056 work that leaked — report it rather than fixing it here, so the fix lands with the increment that owns the seam.
openQuestions: Whether to also assert the mirror-image rule — that no L2 file declares a module-level mutable binding intended as a seam slot (`let configured…`, `export let …`). It would catch a re-singletoning that avoided the configure* name entirely. Planned as NOT in scope: the regex would be noisy against legitimate module state (caches, memos) and a noisy tripwire gets disabled. Raise it again only if a real regression slips through the parameter-shape rule.

Whether services/ is too broad a walk root — it contains set-agnostic session/records implementations that have no configure* exports, so it costs only walk time today. If it ever produces a false positive, narrow the root rather than adding an allow-list entry; an allow-list entry means a seam was exempted from co-residency, which is a decision for Sam.

filesToTouch.what: Add one export beside the existing accessors: `export const policy = () => (store.has(currentSetId()) ? (store.current().policy ?? {}) : {})`, where `store` is the per-set `setKeyed('obligation set')` registry that pp-056 (P-9) installed in this file and `currentSetId` comes from '../../shared/set-context.js'. Deliberately NOT via requireConfiguredSet(): an unresolvable set context, an unconfigured set, or a configured set with no `policy` member all yield {} (empty-safe defaults per §5 P-1), so L2 units that never configure a set stay green. Wrap the currentSetId() call so its FD-17 'No set context' throw (raised only when two or more sets are mounted with no active context) degrades to {} here rather than propagating out of a policy read — record that as a deliberate local softening; every OTHER manifest accessor keeps throwing. No other change to this file (P-9 already keyed it).

OPTION (b), forced by co-residency. Delete the four module-load literal declarations (SYSTEM_POPULATED line 29, ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE lines 31-34, MAX_ENTRIES_FROM lines 41-43, SYSTEM_ANSWER_KEYS line 70) and the SCREAMING_SNAKE export names with them. [])`; `export const enforcedAtContinue = () => new Set(policy().enforcedAtContinue ?? WHY THIS INCREMENT EXISTS, stated plainly: pp-057 (492b7ace) was landed and reported as verified while its own final test:features run was RED at 8 failed / 254 passed (logs/pp-057-test-features-2.log:620). Four of those eight were the real defects repaired here; the other four were the transporter journey specs, which are flaky and pass at HEAD. The orchestrator's landing report for pp-057 quoted the TESTS-repo suite numbers (E2E 152 passed, test:local 127, a11y 11) and never mentioned the frontend's own features leg, so a red ladder step was reported as a green increment. That is a verification failure by the orchestrator, not by the implementor, and it is the SIXTH instance in this build of a green-looking report proving less than it claimed.

HOW THE SWEEP MISSED THEM — this is the reusable lesson. pp-057's acceptance greps were `grep -rn "goto('/')"` and `grep -rn "toHaveURL('/')"`: EXACT matches on the bare root. Every root URL carrying a QUERY STRING — `toHaveURL('/?page=2')` — fails to match those patterns while being exactly the thing the sweep existed to find. One of the four is additionally a multi-line template literal, which no single-line grep catches at all. Generalise: an acceptance grep written as an exact literal proves only that the literal is absent, not that the CLASS is. Anchor on the prefix (`toHaveURL(['\`]/`) and read the hits.

THE CONTACT DEFECT IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE and worth separating: `toHaveAttribute('href', callback)` is not a URL-migration miss, it is a matcher misuse. Playwright's `toHaveAttribute` accepts `string | RegExp`; `toHaveURL` also accepts a `(url: URL) => boolean` predicate. pp-057 used the predicate form on both, so dashboard.e2e.spec.js:50 is correct and contact.e2e.spec.js:57 is not. Anyone repeating the migration on another set should know the two matchers differ.

SCOPE FENCE: two spec files, five assertion sites, nothing else. No production file. No new test. No renamed test. If making the suite green appears to require touching anything outside these two files, STOP and report ok:false — that would mean the diagnosis was wrong.

Both halves are named in pp-007's filesToTouch so nothing is orphaned. The same split applies to co-residency.test.js: born here with the live-animals half and a bootServer({ sets }) seam, completed by pp-007. TWO RISKS THIS INCREMENT MUST RETIRE, NOT ASSUME (§4.1): realm scoping is real (Hapi scopes request-lifecycle extensions added inside a plugin to that plugin's routes — the live-animals entry guard is ALREADY a realm-scoped onPreHandler at routes.js:65-68, so the mechanism is proven in this codebase and onPreAuth simply runs earlier in the same lifecycle), and enterWith survives interleaving. Set charter: CHED-PP scope; the CO-RESIDENCY contract (both gateways register in ONE process; every configure* seam is keyed by set id; a request resolves its set from the owning plugin realm, not from URL parsing; MOUNTS ARE SYMMETRIC — every set is mounted at `'/' + setId`, so live-animals is at /live-animals and plant-products at /plant-products, NO set owns `/`, and `/` is a server-wide 302 to the default set — FD-1/FD-14/FD-15/FD-16 as reversed by R7, plus FD-18/FD-19). Explicitly record that there is NO served-set env var and that the mount prefix is not a per-set choice. Pointers to the SIBLING-SET-PLAN rulings (FD table distilled), the P-2 containment note (future option of retiring the L2 live-animals mapper into sets/live-animals/services/), and the pp-008/pp-010/pp-011 follow-ups this scaffold leaves open.

add-a-set STEP 4. export const plantProducts — Hapi plugin, name 'plant-products' (FD-3). Register body mirrors routes-live-animals.js call-for-call in the LOAD-BEARING order of the §4.4.3 14-row table: (0) `registerSetMount('plant-products', '/plant-products')`, then `server.ext('onPreAuth', (request, h) => { enterSetContext('plant-products'); return h.continue })` as the first extension, with the WHOLE body wrapped in `await withSetContext('plant-products', async () => { … })` so the boot gates read this set; (1) configureObligationSet('plant-products', plantProductsObligationSet) — namespace import carrying .obligations/.groups/.policy; (2) configureFulfilmentRegistry('plant-products', featureEvaluationBindings); (3) NO configureCommodityReference — FD-5: its only consumer is the L2 live-animals mapper, so under per-set keying the plant slot is simply never filled and a plant request that somehow reached that mapper throws loudly instead of mapping with live-animals vocabulary; (4) configureJourneyFlow('plant-products', { sections, taskRows, rowStatus, nextRunTarget, flowOnlyKeys: FLOW_ONLY_KEYS, entryGuardTarget, layout: LAYOUT }); (5) assertObligationPurity(); (6) assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage(); (7) buildDispatch('plant-products', dispatchPages); (8) configureRecords('plant-products', records) — the SET-OWNED impl (FD-5); (9) configureSession('plant-products', session, SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES) — the L2 set-agnostic session impl plus the plant cookie names; (10) registerJourneyCookie(server, { base: '/plant-products', cookieNames: SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES }) so the three plant cookies carry path '/plant-products'; (11) server.ext('onPreHandler', …) entry-guard wrapper verbatim — realm-scoped, so it never fires on live-animals routes; (12) NO countries.prime()/ports.prime() — plant reference data is fixture-backed and the L2 primed caches are live-animals machinery; (13) server.route(allRoutes) with PREFIX-FREE paths (the mount comes from the registration option in router.js).

add-a-set STEP 5. Add `plantProducts` to the existing `import { liveAnimals } from './app/routes.js'` and add ONE new line after the live-animals registration: `await server.register(plantProducts, { routes: { prefix: '/plant-products' } })`. It must be a SEPARATE register call — the prefix option applies to a WHOLE call, so two sets can never share one. R7 SYMMETRY: this line and the live-animals line pp-057 wrote are the same shape with a different set id, and neither passes an empty prefix — if the diff makes them look different, one of them is wrong. Everything else in router.js stays as pp-057 left it: the hoisted unprefixed `server.register([signout])` (FD-19) and the server-wide `GET /` → 302 `/live-animals` (FD-18) are NOT touched, and in particular the plant register must not be folded into an array with either of them.

Add the PLANT HALF to the file pp-006 created, using its bootServer({ sets }) helper — extend, do not rewrite. New cases, all against ONE booted server with BOTH gateways registered (plant via { routes: { prefix: '/plant-products' } }): (a) GET '/live-animals' returns live-animals dashboard content AND GET '/plant-products' returns plant dashboard content that CANNOT render under live-animals, in the same run — note NEITHER is at '/'; (a2) with BOTH sets now registered, GET '/' still 302s to '/live-animals' (FD-18) and GET '/signout', GET '/health' and the static-asset path still resolve UNPREFIXED (FD-19) — pp-006 asserted these with one set; re-assert them with two, because a second prefixed register is exactly the edit that could capture them; (a3) SYMMETRY: assert over the mount registry that both sets are mounted at '/' + their own setId and neither at '' (the same invariant pp-058's tripwire guards; asserting it here too means the co-residency suite fails loudly if a gateway is ever registered asymmetrically); (b) a page from each set resolves its OWN manifest, journey flow, records impl and cookie names — assert the plant response sets plantProducts* cookies at path '/plant-products' and no liveAnimals* cookie, and vice versa; (c) REALM SCOPING, cross-set form: a request to a plant route does NOT execute the live-animals entry guard, and a request to a live-animals route does NOT execute the plant one; (d) ALS INTERLEAVING, cross-set form: one plant and one live-animals request in flight together, the first deliberately awaiting inside its handler, each still reading its own set — a red here is a STOP-and-replan (the contingency is explicit setId threading, a materially larger increment); (e) the P-1 handover from pp-005 — the two sets read DIFFERENT enforcedAtContinue values in this one process; (f) MODE INDEPENDENCE (P-6) — with the plant set on its records stub and live-animals on a fake real client, both serve correctly, and countries.prime()/ports.prime() ran ONCE, on the live-animals gateway only, and was not re-triggered by the plant registration.

Minimal slice of P-4, pulled forward only because lint:arch cannot pass this increment otherwise: add `` `^${APP}/routes-plant-products\\.js$` `` to the routes-is-the-gateway `from.pathNot` allowlist (pp-006 already added routes-live-animals.js). Boot-proof Vitest suite colocated with the gateway, composing the PLANT set alone (FD-17's sole-registered-set fallback applies, so no withSetContext plumbing is needed — that is what co-residency.test.js is for). With PLANT_PRODUCTS_MODE=stub (vi.stubEnv): create a @hapi/hapi server, register plantProducts with { routes: { prefix: '/plant-products' } } — successful registration proves assertObligationPurity + assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage + buildDispatch accept the m0 skeleton; then server.inject: GET '/plant-products' → 200 plant dashboard; POST the create path → 302 into the new journey's import-type page under /plant-products/notifications/…; GET the import-type page → 200; GET the hub → 200 with the empty task list; GET a guarded journey slug on a fresh journey → 302 to import-type (entry-guard). increments.title: Close the async-boundary blind spot: extend the convention tripwire to un-contexted route handlers, and make co-residency catch it
increments.recipe: No recipe. Raised from pp-007's verification round, which proved a real Hapi async-boundary defect AND proved that neither the pp-058 tripwire nor the co-residency suite catches it.

filesToTouch.what: Add a fourth concern to the tripwire alongside the existing three (set seams, symmetric mounts, server-wide routes): SET-OWNED LIFECYCLE CODE MUST RUN IN ITS SET CONTEXT. The defect class: a set gateway that calls `server.route(allRoutes)` raw, rather than mapping through `routeWithSetContext(SET_ID, route)`, produces handlers that execute outside any set context — because `enterSetContext` uses `storage.enterWith()` in an `onPreAuth` extension and that does not reliably propagate into a lifecycle step Hapi resumes from an earlier async context. With one set mounted this is invisible (the single registered set resolves by default); with two it serves the wrong set's config or 500s. Follow the file's existing idiom exactly — it discovers what it guards from the real source rather than hand-maintaining a list, and it keeps its allow-list empty. Cover three shapes: (1) a set gateway registering routes without the context mapping; (2) a route-level `options.ext` method that is not context-wrapped; (3) the plugin-level entry-guard extension not wrapped in `withSetContext`. THE pp-058 BAR APPLIES IN FULL: for each shape, CONSTRUCT the violating arrangement in the test and assert it is REJECTED. A case that only asserts today's gateways look right is worthless — pp-058's own value came from six of its nineteen cases building the violation.

Add a case that FAILS when route handlers run outside their set context. This is the gap pp-007's verification exposed: with `routeWithSetContext` removed from both gateways, `test:features` went to 261 failed / 1 passed and `router.test.js` failed 500-vs-200, but the ENTIRE co-residency suite — including the interleaving pin that reads currentSetId(), the cookie name and the policy from inside a handler — stayed GREEN. Work out why it is insensitive before writing the fix: the likely cause is that other cases in the file establish an ambient context in the vitest worker (withSetContext/enterSetContext are called freely elsewhere), so a handler that resolves no context of its own still finds a usable one. If that is the cause, the new case must be isolated from that ambient state rather than merely asserting harder. Do NOT weaken or delete the existing interleaving pin — it still proves cross-request isolation, which is a different property; add alongside it and say in the file what each one covers.

specs: No Playwright spec. Both halves are Vitest; the feature suite already catches this defect and is not the gap being closed.
acceptanceCriteria: THE MUTATION IS THE ACCEPTANCE, both halves. Remove the `routeWithSetContext` mapping from `server.route(...)` in BOTH `routes-live-animals.js` and `routes-plant-products.js`, and remove the `withSetContext` wrapper around `journeyEntryGuardTarget` in the live-animals `onPreHandler`. With that mutation in place: at least one case in no-set-singletons.test.js MUST go red, AND at least one case in co-residency.test.js MUST go red. Restore the mutation and the whole suite is green. Report the observed failure message for each. Neither half is done until its own mutation turns it red — a green tripwire under the violation it names is the exact failure this increment exists to fix.

The three violating shapes in the tripwire (raw server.route in a gateway, an un-wrapped route-level ext method, an un-wrapped entry-guard extension) are each CONSTRUCTED in the test and asserted rejected, not merely asserted absent from today's code.
The tripwire's allow-list stays empty, and what it guards is still discovered from the real source rather than a hand-maintained list — the two properties pp-058 established.
The existing co-residency interleaving pin is unchanged and still passes; the new case sits alongside it, and the file states which property each covers.
No production file is modified. The diff is exactly the two test files. If closing the gap appears to need a production change, STOP and report — that would be a different increment.

test:features stays at 262 passed and test:e2e at 3 passed — this increment adds no behaviour.

increments.notes:
WHY THIS EXISTS. pp-007 changed shipped live-animals code from inside a scaffold increment — wrapping every route handler and route-level extension in `withSetContext` — justified as a Hapi async-boundary defect. I refused to land that on a plausible argument and required a mutation. The mutation PROVED the defect: without the wrappers `test:features` is 261 failed / 1 passed (the dashboard 500s and specs time out waiting for it) and `router.test.js` fails 500-vs-200. So the fix is forced, not opportunistic, and it landed with pp-007.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE IS WHAT STAYED GREEN. Under that same mutation the whole co-residency suite passed, including the interleaving pin that reads currentSetId(), the cookie name and the policy from INSIDE a route handler — the case the orchestrator had specifically singled out as strong evidence. And pp-058's convention tripwire, whose entire job is catching seams that are not set-keyed, said nothing. So the two artefacts this programme relies on to prove co-residency both have a blind spot exactly where the first real co-residency defect appeared. That is the seventh instance in this build of a confident-looking test proving less than it claimed.

WHY A STATIC TRIPWIRE IS THE RIGHT SECOND LINE. The feature suite DID catch it, loudly. But the feature suite is slow, needs a server on PORT=3050, and is not what an implementor runs while working. pp-058 exists because the fast in-repo guard is what actually shapes the next gateway someone writes — and every future set added via docs/add-a-set.md will register routes. A tripwire that rejects raw `server.route(allRoutes)` in a gateway makes the mistake impossible to commit rather than merely detectable later.

SHAPE OF THE FIX, from pp-007's verifier: 'A basic version could reject raw `server.route(allRoutes)` calls in set gateways. A stronger version would mark context-wrapped handlers/extensions and inspect captured route registrations, failing any set-owned handler or lifecycle extension without that marker; it should also cover the entry guard.' Prefer the stronger version if it can be done without adding production API purely for testability; if marking requires a production change, take the basic version and say why in notes — a production change to serve a test belongs in its own increment with its own argument.

ALSO WORTH RECORDING: docs/add-a-set.md was corrected by pp-007 (the first increment to execute it end to end) to describe the real gateway/barrel shape and the context boundaries. If this increment changes what a gateway must do, the recipe needs the same treatment — check it and correct it here rather than leaving it describing a weaker rule than the tripwire enforces.

ROLLBACK: `git stash push -u`, never `reset --hard` + `clean -fd`.
openQuestions: Does the same async-boundary hazard apply to any OTHER lifecycle point a set owns — server-level onPreResponse, auth schemes, validation failActions? pp-007 wrapped handlers, route-level ext and the entry guard. If other points exist, they are the same defect class and the tripwire should cover them too.

Should `enterSetContext`/`enterWith` remain at all now that handlers and extensions are explicitly wrapped, or is it redundant belt-and-braces? Removing it is a simplification but only if nothing between onPreAuth and the wrapped points reads the context. Not urgent; decide before m1.

AMENDED FOR RULING R7 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session) — SYMMETRIC MOUNTS. The cloned app-root suites each compose ONE set, and under R7 that set now has a NON-EMPTY mount prefix — which the round-2 plan's clones did not have to think about, because the live-animals originals sat at ''. Consequence for this increment: for every cloned suite, work out per value whether it is a ROUTE SHAPE (declared prefix-free; Hapi supplies the mount; transposes unchanged) or an EMITTED LINK / REDIRECT TARGET (prefix-bearing; must read /plant-products/…). The live-animals original's literals are no longer a safe default for the second kind: a '/' in the original now means '/live-animals'. contract.plant-products.test.js is the clearest case and carries an explicit comment — the paths it POSTs to are route shapes, not links, so they stay prefix-free for both sets; anything it ASSERTS about a redirect is a link and is prefixed. routes.plant-products.test.js's prefix-free assertion (added under R3) is unchanged and is now doubly load-bearing: with both sets prefixed, a hand-prefixed route path serves at /plant-products/plant-products/… and a dropped one at /notifications/…, and both 404 immediately rather than lurking.

AMENDED 2026-08-01 for Sam's ruling R3 (co-residency). Scope is unchanged in shape but three things move. (1) THE sets-not-l1 WIDENING IS NOW MANDATORY AND BIGGER: with two real gateway files plus a barrel, the forbidden-target regex must name all three, and routes.js STAYS whitelisted on routes-is-the-gateway even though a barrel no longer imports sets/** — dropping it would be an unrelated semantic change. (2) shared/set-context.js NEEDS NO RULE. It is ordinary L2: it stores set ids and prefixes handed to it and imports nothing under sets/, so the existing L2 rules already cover it. Adding a bespoke rule would be noise and is explicitly out of scope. (3) THE CLONE RATIONALE CHANGES ENTIRELY — this is the substantive amendment. The round-1 justification was that vitest isolates files into workers and configure* are last-write-wins assignments, so a cloned file could safely re-point the SINGLE-SLOT singletons. Those singletons no longer exist: pp-056 (P-9) keyed every seam by set. The reason to keep separate files is now plain readability and independent failure attribution (FD-10 as revised), and the mechanics are simpler than before — FD-17's sole-registered-set fallback means each clone, composing exactly ONE set, resolves currentSetId() with no context plumbing at all. A clone that needs withSetContext is composing more than one set and is wrong; the ONE file that legitimately needs explicit context is co-residency.test.js (pp-006/pp-007), which is not a clone. What DOES change mechanically in every clone: each configure*/buildDispatch call takes setId as its FIRST argument. The old load-bearing warning survives intact and is still the most likely silent defect here: never compute a set-derived value at module load (contract.test.js does exactly that at line 43, and the global setupFile would make a cloned copy read the LIVE-ANIMALS manifest). Clones still do not call configureCommodityReference — under per-set keying the plant slot is deliberately empty (FD-5/P-2), which is stronger than the round-1 'inert' framing. RETAINED DECISIONS: one-load-per-request.test.js is NOT cloned — verified live, it network-mocks the L2 REAL records adapter against /fulfilments|/notifications|/proposed-notifications, live-animals-only machinery the plant path never executes; the plant analogue belongs to pp-008's adapter tests. The contract clone keeps its completeness-guard test (mechanises T-5's standing rule and is the minimal way to keep an it.each table green at zero cases). IDENTICAL_ALLOWLIST stays set-prefixed. NEW small addition to routes.plant-products.test.js: assert every plant route path is PREFIX-FREE, because under the mount prefix a hand-prefixed path serves at /plant-products/plant-products/… and a dropped one at a bare /notifications/… . Under R7 this is NOT a plant-only failure mode and it does NOT lurk: live-animals is mounted too, so the identical trap exists on both sides and either mistake 404s immediately for whichever set makes it. The assertion belongs in both sets' route suites for the same reason. DEP NOTE: pp-010 depends only on pp-007, which transitively guarantees pp-056/pp-057/pp-006/pp-053 and therefore both gateway files and the keyed seams. Exemplars: src/server/app/{contract,routes,indexed,store-ops,copy-convention,copy-parity}.test.js, test/setup-obligation-set.js, .dependency-cruiser.cjs (routes-is-the-gateway and sets-not-l1 rules), package.json script block.

CORRECTED 2026-08-02 BY THE BUILD, and this correction matters beyond this increment. Two claims above are FALSE and were disproven while pp-010 was implemented. (1) THE SOLE-SET FALLBACK CLAIM IS WRONG: this note says each clone composes exactly one set so `currentSetId()` resolves it with no context plumbing, and that a clone needing explicit context is composing more than one set and is wrong. In fact the GLOBAL SETUP FILE MOUNTS LIVE-ANIMALS, so `currentSetId()` stays live-animals and a clone with no plumbing reads the LIVE-ANIMALS manifest — 49 obligations where the plant manifest is empty. Green and silently wrong, the exact failure class this programme keeps hitting. Every clone must ENTER ITS OWN SET CONTEXT IN ITS HOOKS. The same false claim had propagated into docs/add-a-set.md (the recipe every future set follows) and was corrected there in the same commit. (2) ORDERING: this note lists buildDispatch before configureObligationSet for store-ops; dispatch reads the manifest immediately, so the manifest must be configured FIRST. Both were caught by the implementor and are recorded here so a future planner does not reinstate them.

increments.title: Guard against dead specs: every set's e2e specs must be collected by a Playwright project
increments.recipe: No recipe. Raised from pp-011, which discovered that pp-007's plant e2e specs had never executed.

filesToTouch.what: Add a fifth concern to the convention tripwire: EVERY SET'S E2E SPECS MUST HAVE A RUNNER. The gap, proven by pp-011: `vitest.config.js` excludes `src/server/app/sets/*/journeys/linear/features/**/*.e2e.spec.js`, so a set's e2e specs never run under the unit runner; and until pp-011 no Playwright project collected the plant ones. They sat between the two runners — pp-007 landed green with dead specs, and the accessibility defect one of them would have caught (the plant hub's missing sharedCopy) shipped alongside them. Nothing currently stops a third set repeating this exactly. Discover sets from the real filesystem (`src/server/app/sets/*`) the way the file already discovers gateways from the routes.js barrel, read the real `playwright.config.js` projects, and assert that for every set directory containing at least one `*.e2e.spec.js` there is a project whose `testDir` covers it. Follow the file's established idiom: discover rather than hand-maintain, and keep any new allow-list EMPTY and assert it stays empty. THE pp-058 BAR APPLIES: construct the violation — a set directory with e2e specs and no covering project — and assert it is rejected. A test that only confirms today's two sets are covered would not have caught pp-007 and is therefore worthless for the purpose.

specs: No new spec file. This extends the existing convention tripwire; the diff is one test file.
acceptanceCriteria: THE MUTATION IS THE ACCEPTANCE: temporarily remove the `features-plant-products` project from `playwright.config.js` and the tripwire MUST go red naming the uncovered set. Restore it and the suite is green. Report the observed failure message. A guard that stays green with the project removed is exactly the failure this increment exists to prevent.
The violating arrangement is CONSTRUCTED in the test — a set directory carrying e2e specs with no covering project — and asserted rejected, not merely asserted absent from today's config.
Sets are discovered from the filesystem and projects from the real playwright.config.js; neither is a hand-maintained list. Any new allow-list is empty and asserted empty.

A set with NO e2e specs at all does not fail the guard — the rule is 'specs that exist must have a runner', not 'every set must have e2e specs'. Prove this case too, or the guard blocks the next set's first commit.
No production file changes. The diff is exactly one test file.

npm test green with the new cases; the count rises. lint and lint:arch green. `.dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json` byte-identical (SHA-1 0762285ef5bfdd1f06af6fbea491e5e69b53e19a). test:features:all stays at 272 and test:e2e at 3 — this increment adds no behaviour.

increments.notes:
WHY THIS EXISTS. pp-011 wired the first plant-products Playwright project and immediately found that pp-007's plant e2e specs — dashboard, hub and import-type, ten tests including three axe scans — had NEVER RUN. Vitest excludes them by glob; no Playwright project collected them. So pp-007 reported green having authored dead specs, and the plant hub shipped with an accessibility defect (footer links with empty accessible names, from a missing `sharedCopy`) that its own axe test would have caught on the first execution. pp-011 fixed the defect and the wiring; this increment stops the gap recurring.

WHY A GUARD RATHER THAN A NOTE IN THE RECIPE. The recipe was updated by pp-011 to warn about it, and that is worth having, but a recipe warning is only as strong as the next author's attention. The same argument applied to pp-058 and pp-073: the fast in-repo tripwire is what actually shapes the next gateway someone writes, and it makes the mistake impossible to commit rather than merely detectable later. This programme has now had TWO defects reach a commit specifically because a check existed but ran nothing (pp-007's dead specs here; and see pp-066's `--list` count criterion, written for the same failure mode in the tests repo).

SCOPE DISCIPLINE. One test file. Do not touch `playwright.config.js` or `vitest.config.js` — the mutation on the former is a temporary probe and must be reverted. If the guard cannot be written without a production or config change, STOP and report; that would be a different increment with its own argument.

RELATED, NOT IN SCOPE: the same class of question applies to the tests repo, where pp-066 already carries an explicit `--list`-count criterion for exactly this hazard. No cross-repo work here.

ROLLBACK: `git stash push -u`, never `reset --hard` + `clean -fd`.

OPEN QUESTIONS ANSWERED ON LANDING (2026-08-02), neither acted on. (1) A NON-ZERO COLLECTION CHECK WOULD BE STRICTLY STRONGER AND IS A REAL RESIDUAL GAP: this guard asserts a project's testDir COVERS a set's specs, not that its testMatch actually collects them. Playwright allows project-level testDir/testMatch with testDir inherited from the top level, so a covering testDir with a WRONG testMatch would still collect zero and pass this guard. That is a narrower fault than the one observed (no project at all, which is what bit pp-007) and closing it likely needs Playwright's own discovery invoked from inside Vitest. Deliberately NOT expanded here to avoid stacking a third guard increment ahead of journey work — but it is a known hole, and the tests repo already carries an explicit `--list` count criterion for the same hazard at pp-066. (2) SPEC KINDS: today's axe checks live inside `*.e2e.spec.js` and are therefore covered by this guard, but any FUTURE per-set spec kind that gets its own vitest exclusion carries the identical dead-spec risk, so the guard should be generalised over spec kinds at the point such a suite is introduced rather than pre-emptively.
openQuestions: Should the guard also assert a NON-ZERO collected count per set rather than only that a covering project exists? A project can exist and still collect nothing if its testMatch is wrong. Stronger, but it may need to invoke Playwright's own discovery from inside Vitest, which could be slow or awkward — decide from what the config actually allows.

Does the same dead-spec risk apply to the a11y specs and any future per-set suite the repo adds? If the answer is yes generally, the guard should be phrased over 'spec kinds' rather than hard-coding e2e.

Exports `records` = { create, load, list, has, replaceFulfilment, finalise, amend, cancelAmend, copy, softDelete, clear } implementing the engine port (surface pinned by src/server/app/engine/persistence/records.js) via global fetch against config.js URLs, per the §6.2 op→HTTP table: create(_options) POST notificationsUrl body '{}', expect 201, return marshal(body) — journeyId IS the minted GBN-PP referenceNumber; load({ journeyId }) GET …/{journeyId}, 404→undefined, 200→marshal; list({ page=1, sort='arrivalDate,desc', referenceNumber }) GET with query string, map the page response → { rows: content.map(marshalListItem), page, size, totalElements, totalPages }; has(journeyId) GET → 200 true / 404 false; replaceFulfilment(journeyId, fulfilment, { known }={}) — resolve status (use `known` when supplied else GET), assert writable (draft|amend else throw), body = toDto(projectAnswers(structuredClone(fulfilment ?? {}))), PUT …/{journeyId}, 200|201 → marshal; finalise/amend/cancelAmend/softDelete via PUT …/{journeyId}/status with {status:'SUBMITTED'} / {status:'AMEND'} / {status:'SUBMITTED', discardChanges:true} / {status:'DELETED'}; clear() throws 'records.clear is not supported in real mode'. **COPY — R4, the change of record for this increment:** `copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey)` POSTs …/{journeyId}/copies with the header `Idempotency-Key: <idempotencyKey>` ALWAYS set, expects 201 and marshals the new documentless DRAFT. The key is REQUIRED: reject a missing/blank key locally, before any request, with a clear error ('Idempotency-Key must not be blank' — the same voice the live-animals backend uses), so a caller that forgets it fails loudly at the seam instead of minting duplicate drafts. The engine port already carries the key — engine/journey.js copyJourney(request, h, journeyId, idempotencyKey) — so this is a straight transposition of the live-animals frontend behaviour (services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js sends the header) onto the NOTIFICATION resource. TRANSPOSE THE PATTERN, NOT THE CODE: live-animals implements idempotency on the FULFILMENT resource; here /copies hangs off the notification. Every non-ok response (other than the handled 404s) throws via a failed(operation, response) helper; all requests send content-type application/json + the tracing header. Helpers stay inside real.js — records/ is flat per the plan's §1 tree.

Op→HTTP contract unit test: mock global fetch at the NETWORK boundary (same technique as L2 real.requests.test.js — never module-mock). One test per op asserting method, URL (incl. query-string shape for list), body (create sends '{}'; replaceFulfilment body has NO server-set fields; status ops send exactly {status} / {status, discardChanges:true}) and the marshalled return shape. R4 cases: copy sends the Idempotency-Key header with exactly the value passed in; copy with a missing/blank key throws BEFORE issuing any fetch (assert zero fetch calls by observing that no request was recorded, not by call-spying on a module); a repeated copy with the SAME key still issues the request (dedupe is the server's job in real mode) and marshals whatever the backend returns. Negative paths: load/has 404 → undefined/false; non-ok elsewhere throws naming the op; replaceFulfilment against SUBMITTED/DELETED throws without issuing the PUT; clear throws.

Upgrade the pp-007 boot-minimum stub to full semantic parity with real. In-memory Map keyed by journeyId; per-record { journeyId, status, createdAt, submittedAt, fulfilment, submittedSnapshot? }. Reference minting: GBN-PP-{YY}-{6 Crockford base32 chars} matching ^GBN-PP-\d{2}-[0-9A-HJ-KM-NP-TV-Z]{6}$. Status-transition legality mirroring the backend §3.1 table exactly: finalise only from draft|amend → submitted (sets submittedAt, drops snapshot); amend only from submitted → amend (captures submittedSnapshot); cancelAmend only from amend with a snapshot → restores fulfilment+submittedAt, back to submitted; softDelete from draft|submitted|amend → deleted, idempotent; anything else throws. replaceFulfilment guards writable (draft|amend) and stores a structuredClone. list hides deleted, 1-based paging with the same envelope as real, referenceNumber filter. clear() empties the store AND its dedupe index. **COPY — R4:** `copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey)` mirrors the real contract with a DEDUPE KEY: reject a missing/blank key with the same error real.js raises; keep a Map from the dedupe key to the minted copy's journeyId and RETURN THE EXISTING COPY on a repeat rather than minting a second draft — the live-animals reference behaviour (FulfilmentService.copy() looks up findByCopyIdempotencyKey first and returns the existing copy, re-checking after a DuplicateKeyException). Scope the dedupe key to the SOURCE REFERENCE (`${journeyId}:${idempotencyKey}`), so the same key used against a different source notification legitimately mints a new draft — that is the live-animals unique-partial-index semantic ('copy_idempotency_key' over copyIdempotencyKey) transposed. The copy is a fresh DRAFT with a new ref, documentless, carrying no submittedSnapshot/submittedAt (D-19).

Pins the stub-only semantics not covered by the shared port suite: minted refs match the GBN-PP pattern and are unique; the five-row transition-legality table (each illegal transition throws); amend snapshot capture then cancelAmend restore round-trip; list paging/filter/deleted-hidden; clear resets store and dedupe index. R4 cases: copy with a blank key throws; two copies of the same source with the SAME key return ONE draft (same journeyId, and the store holds exactly one new record); two copies of the same source with DIFFERENT keys mint two drafts; the same key against a DIFFERENT source mints a new draft (dedupe is scoped to the source reference); a copy does not share mutable state with its source.

Rewrite as the stub/real switch (mirror L2 services/persistence/records/index.js verbatim): import { isRealMode } from '../mode.js'; import { records as stubRecords } from './stub.js'; import { records as realRecords } from './real.js'; export const records = isRealMode() ? realRecords : stubRecords. Standing home for every later increment's mapping + omission tests.

Dual-implementation engine-port contract suite, pattern copied from L2 src/server/app/services/persistence/records/records-port.test.js (read it first and mirror its structure): ONE shared spec run against BOTH the stub and the network-mocked real impl, proving identical observable semantics — create returns a draft with a journeyId; load round-trips what replaceFulfilment saved; has true/false; finalise→submitted, amend→amend, cancelAmend restores the submitted fulfilment, softDelete→deleted idempotent; replaceFulfilment on a non-writable record rejects. **R4 — the two copy-idempotency pins the ruling names, and they are the reason this suite is load-bearing for pp-045:** (1) 'one new draft per idempotency key' — copying the same source twice with the same key yields ONE new draft (the second call returns the first copy's journeyId), and twice with different keys yields two; (2) 'copy idempotency scoped to the source reference' — the same key against a different source notification mints a new draft. Under the network-mocked real impl these are asserted at the request level (the header is sent verbatim on every call and the server's response is trusted); under the stub they are asserted at the semantic level (the dedupe index dedupes). Record in the file header that real-mode dedupe is only genuinely enforced once the backend honours the header — see openQuestions.

Extend the standing co-residency suite (created pp-006, plant half pp-007) with the RECORDS-SEAM case this increment makes provable: in ONE booted server with both gateways registered, a plant request resolves the SET-OWNED plant records impl while a live-animals request resolves the L2 live-animals impl — assert through observable behaviour (a plant create mints a GBN-PP-pattern reference; a live-animals create mints its own reference shape; neither appears in the other's list) rather than by inspecting the registry. (1) THE RECORDS SEAM IS KEYED BY SET. configureRecords now takes setId as its first argument (pp-056/P-9), so the plant impl is not 'the' records impl but 'the plant records impl' — and that is now PROVABLE rather than conventional: co-residency.test.js gains a case showing a plant request resolving the set-owned impl while a live-animals request resolves the L2 one, in one process, with neither set's notifications visible to the other. The P-2 containment claim likewise strengthens from 'we do not call configureCommodityReference on the plant path' to 'the plant slot is ABSENT, so a plant request reaching the L2 mapper throws loudly instead of silently mapping with live-animals vocabulary' — added as a negative test. (2) R4 LANDS HERE, NOT WITH THE COPY BUTTON. The round-1 plan of this increment explicitly sent NO Idempotency-Key on POST …/copies and raised it as an open question. Sam has ruled: match what live-animals already does, exactly, on both sides, sequenced BEFORE pp-045 ships the Copy button. Live-animals reference implementation, for transposition: BACKEND — FulfilmentController.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY = 'Idempotency-Key' as a REQUIRED @RequestHeader, blank rejected with BadRequestException('Idempotency-Key must not be blank'); Fulfilment carries copyIdempotencyKey with a unique PARTIAL index (name 'copy_idempotency_key', def {'copyIdempotencyKey':1}, partialFilter {'copyIdempotencyKey':{'$type':'string'}}); FulfilmentService.copy() looks up findByCopyIdempotencyKey FIRST and returns the existing copy on a repeat, re-checking after a DuplicateKeyException. FRONTEND — a randomUUID() minted per RENDERED copy action (features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js and features/check-answers/controller.js), carried in a hidden input named idempotencyKey, sent as the Idempotency-Key header by services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js, mirrored in the stub adapter with a dedupe key, with records-port contract tests pinning 'one new draft per idempotency key' and 'copy idempotency scoped to the source reference'. **TRANSPOSE THE PATTERN, NOT THE CODE:** live-animals implements this on the FULFILMENT resource; the plant-products design puts /copies on the NOTIFICATION resource, so the dedupe key is scoped to the source NOTIFICATION reference and the stored key belongs on the notification document. THIS increment owns the frontend half — adapter, stub dedupe, port contract tests. pp-045 owns only the UI half (mint per rendered action, hidden input, pass through copyJourney) and its increment body now says so. The BACKEND half is a REQUIRED, currently-unplanned work item: the Phase-B /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies endpoint as built by pp-001 accepts no such header, so real-mode dedupe is not yet enforced server-side — see openQuestions; the frontend contract is nonetheless complete and stub-proven, and the header is sent unconditionally so the backend change is additive. increments.title: Frontend: copy idempotency on the plant records port — Idempotency-Key in real + stub, records-port contract tests, rendering contract for the Copy button (R4)
increments.recipe: No recipe covers a records adapter (SIBLING-SET-PLAN §8 G-D). The script is a TRANSPOSITION of the live-animals implementation named file-by-file in notes, per Sam's ruling R4. NOTE THE TRANSPOSITION: live-animals implements idempotency on the FULFILMENT resource (POST /fulfilments/{id}/copy); plant-products puts /copies on the NOTIFICATION resource (POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies). Transpose the pattern, not the code.

filesToTouch.what: Change the copy op from `copy(journeyId)` to `copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey)` and send the header. Exemplar to mirror: services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js:15-20, where copy issues the POST with `'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey` merged into the request headers alongside the existing content-type and tracing headers. Plant form: POST `${notificationsUrl}/${journeyId}/copies` with headers { 'content-type': 'application/json', [tracingHeader]: …, 'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey }, expect 201, return marshal(body). ADD A LOCAL GUARD BEFORE THE FETCH: if idempotencyKey is nullish or, after String(...).trim(), empty, throw new Error('records.copy requires an idempotencyKey') — do NOT let a keyless copy reach the network. That guard is load-bearing beyond hygiene: it is what makes it impossible for pp-045 to ship a Copy button that mints no key (the backend would 400, but a local throw fails in unit tests rather than only in an integration run). This edit CLOSES pp-008's recorded open question 'POST …/copies has no Idempotency-Key support' — pp-054 adds it to the backend, so the frontend now sends it.

Change the stub's copy op to `copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey)` with a dedupe map, mirroring services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/create.js:22-27 exactly. Add a module-level `copiesBySourceAndKey = new Map()` beside the existing journeys store (and clear it in clear(), which the stub already exposes as a test hook). Behaviour: build `const dedupeKey = `${journeyId}\u0000${idempotencyKey}`` — the NUL separator is deliberate and is the live-animals form; it makes the composite key unambiguous for any journeyId/key pair. If copiesBySourceAndKey has that dedupeKey, return a structuredClone of the ALREADY-MADE copy and make no new record. Otherwise run the existing copy path (source lookup, copyable-status guard, mint a fresh GBN-PP reference, fresh DRAFT, cloned content, no submittedAt/submittedSnapshot — documentless per D-19), then copiesBySourceAndKey.set(dedupeKey, newRecord.journeyId) before returning. Apply the SAME blank-key guard as real.js (throw before any store read) so the two impls fail identically — that identity is what the port contract suite asserts.

Add the two R4 contract cases to the dual-implementation suite pp-008 created (the suite already runs one shared spec against BOTH the stub and the network-mocked real impl — add these inside it so both impls are held to them):
(1) 'one new draft per idempotency key' — create a source, transition it to a copyable status, call copy(sourceRef, key) TWICE with the same key, assert both calls return the SAME journeyId and that a subsequent list() shows exactly ONE draft copy of that source. Not 'copy was called once' — assert the observable record count, because that is the behaviour the backend index enforces.
(2) 'copy idempotency scoped to the source reference' — with the same key value, copy(sourceA, key) and copy(sourceB, key) must yield DISTINCT journeyIds, each derived from its own source. READ THE OPEN QUESTION BEFORE WRITING THIS ONE: the plant BACKEND (pp-054) dedupes on the key ALONE, matching live-animals, while the stub's `${journeyId}\u0000${key}` composite is source-scoped. The two agree in production only because a key is minted fresh per rendered action per source, so the same key never reaches two sources. Resolution for this suite: assert source scoping against the STUB, and for the real impl assert the weaker, true statement — that the request carries the key and the path carries the source reference, so the server can scope however it chooses. Mark the divergence with a comment naming pp-054's openQuestion so the next person does not 'fix' the stub to match a backend that may itself change.
Also add: copy() with a missing/blank key rejects in BOTH impls before any request or store write.

Add to the network-boundary op→HTTP suite: the copy request carries an `Idempotency-Key` header whose value is exactly the argument passed (assert on the captured fetch init, not on a spy call count); the header is present alongside the existing content-type and tracing headers; and copy() with a nullish or whitespace-only key throws WITHOUT issuing a fetch (assert the fetch mock recorded zero calls — 'did not go to the network' is the behaviour under test).

Add to the stub-only suite: repeating copy(sourceRef, key) with the same key returns the same journeyId and leaves the store size unchanged; two different keys against one source yield two distinct drafts; clear() empties the dedupe map as well as the journeys store (otherwise a later test inherits a stale copy and fails mysteriously); a blank key throws before any store mutation.

Add a short '## Copy idempotency' section to the set charter recording the RENDERING CONTRACT that the Copy button must follow when pp-045 ships it, so the requirement survives outside this increment's diff. State it as four rules, each naming its live-animals exemplar: (1) a `randomUUID()` from node:crypto is minted PER RENDERED COPY ACTION — per row on the dashboard, per render of the review page — never once per module load and never once per process (exemplars: features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:1,22 mints inside the per-row action builder; features/check-answers/controller.js:1,73 takes `copyIdempotencyKey = randomUUID()` as a defaulted option so a re-render can pass the SAME key back in); (2) the key rides the form as a hidden input named exactly `idempotencyKey` (exemplars: the dashboard and check-answers template.njk files); (3) the copy POST controller reads `request.payload?.idempotencyKey?.trim()` and passes it as the fourth argument of `copyJourney(request, h, journeyId, idempotencyKey)` — the L2 engine seam already carries it (engine/journey.js:125, verified; NO L2 change is needed for plant-products); (4) the recoverable-error path re-renders with the SAME key, not a new one, so a user retrying after a 500 gets the copy that may already have been made (exemplar: features/notification-actions/controller.js:12-24, recoverCopy). Add a FIFTH rule (R7 — symmetric mounts): the Copy button's form ACTION and its post-copy REDIRECT are prefix-BEARING LINKS, built with pagePath()/hubPath()/dashboardPath(), never route-shape builders and never a hand-written path. The live-animals exemplar being transposed (features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js) emits paths for a set that is ITSELF prefixed now, so a bare `/notifications/…` or a bare `'/'` copied across would be wrong for BOTH sets — under FD-18 a bare '/' would even 302 the user into live-animals after copying a plant draft. Say this in the charter so pp-045's planner meets it before writing the action. Also record that sets/plant-products/services/records/{real,stub}.js THROW on a missing key, so a Copy button that forgets rule 1 fails in unit tests rather than silently double-creating.

AMENDED FOR RULING R7 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session) — SYMMETRIC MOUNTS. One small but real consequence for this increment, and it is entirely in the charter contract rather than in the adapter code: the Copy button's form ACTION and its post-copy REDIRECT are prefix-BEARING LINKS (pagePath/hubPath/dashboardPath), not route shapes. The live-animals file being transposed (features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js) now emits `/live-animals/…` rather than the bare `/notifications/…` it emitted when live-animals sat at the root, so a literal copy-across would be wrong for both sets — and a bare '/' redirect would 302 a user who just copied a PLANT draft into live-animals (FD-18). The charter gains that as rule 5 so pp-045's planner meets it. Nothing about the Idempotency-Key work itself changes: headers, dedupe keys and the port contract are URL-agnostic.

RULING R4 (Sam, 2026-08-01): copy idempotency matches what live-animals already does, exactly, on both sides, and is sequenced BEFORE the Copy button ships. pp-054 is the backend half; this is the frontend half. BOTH must land before pp-045 (draft lifecycle), which is the increment that renders the Copy button — say this in pp-045's body when it is planned, and treat a Copy action arriving without both as a build-loop halt.

SCOPE SPLIT AND WHY (headless decision, recorded not asked). The orchestrator's brief for this increment names four things: randomUUID per rendered copy action, the hidden idempotencyKey input, the Idempotency-Key header in the adapter, and the records-port contract tests. Only the last two can be BUILT here, because there is no rendered copy action in the plant set yet: pp-037 (dashboard, full build) explicitly limits pass-1 row actions to Continue-into-hub and defers delete/amend/copy-as-new to pp-045, and pp-045 is one of the m5 increments that ruling R5 says stay unplanned stubs — so this increment must not plan it. The resolution is not to drop the rendering half but to make it UNSKIPPABLE: real.js and stub.js both throw on a missing key, so any future Copy button that forgets to mint one fails in unit tests, and the four-rule rendering contract is written into the set charter (sets/plant-products/docs/README.md) where pp-045's planner will read it. If Sam would rather see the rendered action built now, the change is to pull the dashboard copy row action forward out of pp-045 into this increment — flagged, not assumed.

- engine/journey.js:125-127 — copyJourney(request, h, journeyId, idempotencyKey) → records.copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey) (the L2 seam ALREADY carries the key; nothing in L2 changes)

increments.notes:
AMENDED FOR RULING R7 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session) — SYMMETRIC MOUNTS. Two consequences for this increment, both about the entry guard and both cited to SIBLING-SET-PLAN §4.6 A rows 4-7. (1) The plant guard builds its journey prefix from setBase() PER REQUEST ('/plant-products/notifications/'), never from a module-load const — unchanged in substance, but the contrast case in its unit pin changes: the other context now yields '/live-animals/notifications/', not '/notifications/', because no set sits at the root. (2) NEW AND BEHAVIOURAL: `request.path` under a Hapi mount prefix INCLUDES the prefix, so the guard's startsWith test and its slice-based journey-id extraction must both use the prefixed value. This is the same trap pp-057 fixes for live-animals; here it is a build-it-right-first-time requirement rather than a migration, and it gets its own pin. Session cookies are symmetric too: plantProducts* at path /plant-products, liveAnimals* at path /live-animals — so 'a plant draft is invisible to live-animals and vice versa' is enforced by the cookie path itself on both sides, and the co-residency cases assert it in both directions.

AMENDED 2026-08-01 for Sam's ruling R3 (co-residency). This increment now sits DOWNSTREAM OF THE SESSION-SEAM REWORK, and three things change in consequence. (1) COOKIE NAMES ARE ACCESSORS, NOT CONSTANTS. By the time this runs, pp-056 has converted engine/persistence/session.js's three EXPORTED MUTABLE bindings (KNOWN_JOURNEYS_COOKIE / OPENING_RUN_COOKIE / FLOW_ONLY_ANSWERS_COOKIE) into knownJourneysCookie() / openingRunCookie() / flowOnlyAnswersCookie() resolving the current set's cookieNames. Nothing in this increment imports the old bindings, and anything that reads a cookie name reads it through the accessor. (2) THE PLANT COOKIES ARE PATH-SCOPED. routes-plant-products.js calls registerJourneyCookie(server, { base: '/plant-products', cookieNames: SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES }), so the three plant cookies carry path '/plant-products' while live-animals' carry '/live-animals' (R7 — pp-057 moved them off '/', which invalidated existing sessions; the two sets are symmetric here, neither is at the root). That makes 'a journey started in one set is invisible to the other' a testable claim, and it is now an acceptance criterion and an E2E scenario rather than an assumption. (3) THE ENTRY GUARD IS REALM-SCOPED AND MUST BE SHOWN NOT TO FIRE ON LIVE-ANIMALS ROUTES. Hapi scopes request-lifecycle extensions to the registering plugin's routes; the live-animals entry guard is already a realm-scoped onPreHandler, which is the precedent. This increment adds the behavioural pin in both directions. FOURTH AND MOST IMPORTANT: THE SET'S ENTRY GUARD MUST USE THE FUNCTION FORM OF THE JOURNEY PREFIX. `const JOURNEY_PREFIX = `${BASE}/notifications/`` — the live-animals shape — is a module-load capture and is exactly the bug class the URL work (pp-057) exists to remove; under co-residency it would bind the wrong set's base or none at all. The plant guard therefore builds its prefix from setBase() on every call, and a unit pin proves the same function yields different prefixes under different set contexts. dependsOn stays [pp-007, pp-008]; pp-056/pp-057 (P-9/P-10) are covered transitively through pp-007→pp-006. Division of labour vs pp-017 unchanged: this increment owns MECHANICS (guard, opening run, session commit, resume); pp-017 owns the full page spec. Guard unit tests still need a non-empty manifest to prove hasCommittedNotificationAnswers=true — compose a fixture set via configureObligationSet(setId, …) (bridge characterisation-test pattern), noting the seam now takes a setId first. Rulings applied: R3, FD-3 (plantProducts* cookie names, now load-bearing), FD-8, FD-13, FD-14/FD-15/FD-16/FD-17, §4.2 rows 6/8/10/11, c-018/c-004/c-014 recorded once in docs/README.md. Exemplars (transpose, do not invent): sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/entry-guard.js (policy shape — but NOT its JOURNEY_PREFIX const), flow/run.js, features/import-type-filter/controller.js, and shared/paths.js + shared/set-context.js as pp-056/pp-057 landed them.

filesToTouch.what: STEP 1. `git -C ~/git/defra/trade-imports-animals/repos/trade-imports-animals-tests branch --show-current` must print `spike/trace-to-requirements`. If not, STOP.

NEW. Mirrors `adapters/http/notification-api-client.ts` (verified live, 60 lines) in SHAPE, not in endpoints. It reuses the shared transport unchanged: `import { RestClient } from '@adapters/http/rest-client'`, `getBackendBaseUrl()` / `getDeveloperApiKey()` from `@config/service-base-urls`, and the same `constructor(request: APIRequestContext, baseUrl = getBackendBaseUrl(), apiKey = getDeveloperApiKey())` signature.

METHODS, straight from SIBLING-SET-PLAN §6.2's call table (base `/plant-products/notifications`):
- `create()` → `POST /plant-products/notifications` with a blank referenceNumber; 201 body carries the server-minted `GBN-PP-…` ref
- `load(ref)` → `GET /plant-products/notifications/{ref}` (response EMBEDS `accompanyingDocuments`)
- `list(params)` → `GET /plant-products/notifications?page&sort&referenceNumber` — page is 1-BASED, DELETED hidden server-side
- `has(ref)` → the same GET, 200 → true / 404 → false
- `replace(ref, body)` → `PUT /plant-products/notifications/{ref}` (whole-document, last-write-wins)
- `setStatus(ref, body)` → `PUT …/{ref}/status`; `{ status: 'SUBMITTED' }` = finalise, `{ status: 'AMEND' }` = amend, `{ status: 'SUBMITTED', discardChanges: true }` = cancel-amend, `{ status: 'DELETED' }` = soft delete (idempotent)

WHAT THIS REPO ADDS OVER THE FRONTEND'S OWN SPECS: the frontend's in-repo `*.e2e.spec.js` run against a self-hosted server on the records STUB. WHY THE ENTRY-GUARD SPEC IS THE MOST VALUABLE FILE IN THIS INCREMENT: co-residency puts two entry guards in one process, each realm-scoped by FD-15. Two files named `import-type-page.ts` under different set dirs is the intended outcome, not duplication to be refactored away — the plant page has different copy, different options and a different next page.

filesToTouch.what: Make minEntries/maxEntries cardinality for a nested group evaluate per immediate parent instance rather than once over the global record list. Top-level groups retain the existing single aggregate error. Nested errors carry the parent fulfilment id as instanceId and the count for only that parent; use the group's within implication records as the parent worklist. Preserve anyOfIds, allOrNothingOfIds and recordCountEquals semantics unchanged.

Include nested minEntries/maxEntries cardinality errors when rolling a parent entry's completeness. A lines instance with zero required species must be incomplete even when its own mandatory line leaf is filled. Keep optional empty varieties complete and retain the direct mandatory-leaf check for a positional empty variety.

Validate every numeric ancestor in collectionPath against the current positional answer tree before appendEntryAt/updateEntryAt/removeEntryAt calls setAt. An absent, non-integer or out-of-range parent is rejected without calling replaceJourneyFulfilment: append returns null and update/remove remain no-ops. This prevents sparse fulfilments being saved before projectAnswers throws.

Flip the four pp-012 it.fails contracts to ordinary tests without changing their names or assertions: species minEntries per line, missing species rolling up to line incomplete, and clean rejection at each of the two out-of-range ancestor levels.

Add focused depth-2 regression coverage for per-parent min/max counting, parent completeness rollup and mutation rejection so the generic behavior is pinned below the pp-012 integrated fixture. Do not alter existing assertions, expectations or test names.

increments.notes: pp-012 proved the failure is generic L2 behavior, not plant-products modeling. The evaluator enumerates depth-3 paths correctly, but checkMinEntries/checkMaxEntries count the whole nested group globally and emit no parent identity. collection-complete only consults per-instance anyOf errors, so it cannot see a nested collection floor. The write path calls setAt before validating either ancestor; replaceJourneyFulfilment persists line5/species0/variety0 or line0/species9/variety0, then projectAnswers rejects the sparse indices, leaving storage already replaced. (b) action='search-species' — Joi: required -> 'Enter a genus and species' (400); else re-render with server-built species results (genus/species substring match over the fixture, each result showing genusAndSpecies + its commodity code, with a per-result Add submit named add-species-<speciesId>). (c) add-species-<speciesId> submit — resolve the species in the fixture (refuse forged/stale ids: unknown id re-renders 400), duplicate-code guard as in (a), then append the line ({ commoditySelection: <code> }) AND seed its first species entry via state.appendEntryAt(request, h, ['commodityLines', newIndex, 'species'], { eppoCode, genusAndSpecies }) with parent-index validation (Number.isInteger && in range) before the nested write — eppoCode is THE join key; the add-species-<id> submit name is TRANSIENT UI state and is never committed. (d) tree leaf select — submit name select-code with value=<leafCode>, same append+duplicate path as (a); tree DRILL-DOWN is plain GET links (?parent=<code>), never a POST (fixes the legacy buttons-as-links anti-pattern). Everything RENDERED or REDIRECTED TO uses the PREFIX-BEARING link builders resolved per request: the tree drill-down anchors are pagePath(journeyId, page.slug) + '?parent=<code>' (never a hand-written '/notifications/…' string — under symmetric mounts NO set is registered at prefix '', so a dropped mount 404s loudly rather than silently landing on another set; that visible failure is exactly why R7 reversed the asymmetric scheme), the form action and back link likewise, and kit.nextTarget's target already carries the mount.

Not platform-touching (all edits inside sets/plant-products/ + the plant contract table), so the two-sided co-residency check (both sets serving correctly under their own prefixes from one process) is not mandated — npm test in the ladder still exercises the shared L1/L2 suites.
