increments.notes: 1:1 carry of inc-017 per MAPPING.json: a read-only echo of the commodityLines collection — NO new data captured, no new obligations, meta.collects = []. Primary recipe add-a-page for the registration spine, with the add-a-collection loop-page steps (§4.5/§4.7 of the cheat-sheet) governing the Remove branch; exemplar file-for-file is the live-animals consignment-details page (collects:[], per-row Remove submit inside the same POST, remove/post-remove.js action parsing — verified live this session, including its contract case at contract.test.js:213-222 which this increment's contract.plant-products.test.js case mirrors). DECISIONS (headless, recorded): (1) Remove operates at the SPECIES-row level — removeEntryAt(['commodityLines', i, 'species'], j) — matching the legacy remove_species_<id> semantics; the 'line's per-instance identity' in the planning brief is honoured as the row's (lineIndex, speciesIndex) pair validated at two levels per §8 G-B before any write. Whole-commodity-line removal is NOT offered on this page (legacy offers none; deselection of a code happens via commodity-search's reconcile, pp-023). (2) Cannot-remove-last parity kept: Remove suppressed when a line has one species ({{#gt variations.length 1}} in the legacy template). (3) One row per species; multiple varieties stack inside the Variety/Class cells (legacy complements were species-level rows; our depth-3 model can hold several varieties per species — stacking keeps 1 row = 1 removable entity, avoiding several Remove buttons with identical effect). (4) GOV.UK toolbox rulings from the page spec's nonStandardPatterns applied: govukTable macro (legacy hand-rolled table dropped govuk-table__row and carried the govuk-!margin-bottom-9 typo), no link-button class in either direction (Remove is an honest secondary submit button; 'Add another commodity' uses the Button component's href form), govuk-!-text-align-right over bespoke text-align-right, visually-hidden actions header renamed 'Actions' (legacy 'Remove action links' was a misnomer — they are buttons). (5) Blank Variety/Class cells, never the legacy 'None' literal (GDS content ruling flagged in the page spec; 'None' only reaches the cell when the fixture actually offers it as a variety option, in which case its label renders like any other). (6) No max-lines notice: SIBLING-SET-PLAN §3.3 declares policy.maxEntriesFrom = {} for CHED-PP, so the legacy cap state (env-configured, never traced) is deliberately not ported. (7) No check-answers work (pp-038), no mapper change (removal rides the existing whole-document PUT via pp-008's records service), no client JS, no webpack entry. (8) Continue label 'Save and continue' kept verbatim from the confirmed trace; the legacy three-way save routing (commodity_summary.js:47-53) is NOT ported — kit.nextTarget + section order own navigation here. Depth-3 reads/writes sit on P-7-proven ground (pp-012 gate) behind the pp-021 model-extension review.
openQuestions: Legacy renders this page ONLY when the chosen species carries variety/class reference data (the page-spec's central open question — 1 of 59 traced journeys reached it, and the spec recommends one deliberate trace: 08059000/CIDAC with no class chosen). This increment places the page unconditionally in the commodities section order per the plan's §2.1 page list; whether it should instead be conditionally skipped (or dropped in favour of the review page) is a design decision for the pp-021-adjacent review to confirm.

The legacy Remove control was never rendered in any trace and never exercised by any E2E test (template-inferred only); the cannot-remove-last suppression and immediate-removal-without-confirmation behaviours are therefore ported from template reading, not observed behaviour. The no-confirmation destructive remove matches the documents exemplar's house pattern, but flag for content/design review.

The 'Add another Genus (and Species)' link needs a line-context mechanism into commodity-basic-description; this plan defers to whatever line-targeting shape pp-024 shipped (query param vs path segment) — the implementor must match it exactly rather than invent a second convention.

increments.title: commodity-bulk-details — per-commodity measures
increments.recipe: sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-collection.md (batch-split details page over an existing collection — the consignment-details exemplar; page registration steps per sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-page.md)

filesToTouch.what: Add export const commodityBulkDetailsPage = { id: 'commodity-bulk-details', slug: 'commodity-bulk-details' }. File stays import-free (controller/flow both import the same object).

export const meta = { ...commodityBulkDetailsPage, collects: [] } (the commodityLines root is owned by commodity-search; members inherit dispatch coverage from the group — exemplar: live-animals consignment-details.controller.js:29). GET: state.get() once; state.collectionView(answers, ['commodityLines']) for facts; build per-line view rows (code + ref-data description from the pp-014 commodities service) prefilled from each entry's nine measure leaves; empty bulk panel. POST branches on the named submit action (documents-exemplar pattern — action travels as a submit button value so the crumb rides along, no GET mutation): (a) action='apply' — validate ≥1 line checkbox selected ('Select at least one commodity line to apply changes to') and ≥1 of the six bulk fields filled ('Fill in at least one field to update the selected commodity lines'); each FILLED bulk value also passes its field's format rule; then COPY each filled value onto every selected line via state.updateEntryAt(request, h, ['commodityLines'], index, entry) per selected index (copy-per-line, never apportion — v16 ruling) and 302 back to this page (server round-trip, zero client JS); bulk values are UI only, never persisted as answers. (b) action='clear' — re-render with an empty bulk panel, per-line values untouched (fixes the legacy Clear-by-reload trap; no write). (c) default Save and continue — validate EVERY line's measures with lib/validate factories (canonical strings in copyKeys); invalid → 400 re-render raw values; valid → commit each line in place via state.updateEntryAt wrapped in kit.recoverableSave (marked failure → recoverableError re-render 500; unexpected errors throw); exit via await kit.nextTarget(request, page, committed.scope) with kit.hubExitTarget(request) winning first. NEW. Collects `commodityInputMethod` (MANUAL | CSV). FD-8 is explicit that this is NOT flow-only — it PERSISTS on the document (`commodity.inputMethod`, SCHEMA-DESIGN §1.1), which is the opposite of `importType`. The spec below must assert that difference, because it is the kind of thing a reader assumes wrongly by analogy. CSV is an m5 branch; at m3 only MANUAL continues anywhere, so the page object exposes both options and the spec asserts the CSV branch's current behaviour rather than pretending it does not exist.

NEW. The commodity-code picker. Collects `commoditySelection` — the code chosen here maps to `commodityCode` PLUS a ref-data-derived `commodityDescription` (§3.1). Locators: the search input, the result list, a `result(code)` locator, the no-results state, and the error summary. Values come from `domain/plant-products/constants/commodity-codes.ts` (pp-061) — real fixture codes, never invented.

NEW. The per-line leaves: `numberOfPackages`, `packageType`, `quantity`, `quantityType`, `netWeight`, `controlledAtmosphereContainer`, `finishedOrPropagated`, `intendedForFinalUsers`, `testAndTrial` (§3.1 `commodities/lines.js`). Nine fields — expose each individually plus a `fill(values)` convenience that mirrors ONE UI submit, so the flow can drive a line without the spec listing nine calls.

NEW. The species and variety leaves. Species (`within: commodityLines`): `eppoCode` — THE JOIN KEY (§3.1) — and `genusAndSpecies` (ref-data-derived). Varieties (`within: species`, optional): `variety` (store the ID, NOT the display label — Open Q 2 ruling) and `varietyClass` (allow-listed per species: CLASS_I | CLASS_II | EXTRA_CLASS, null when N/A).

Expose an `addAnother` control and a per-entry `remove(index)` control if the built page has them — the remove path is what the depth-3 feature spec exercises.

NEW. The add-another loop's summary. This is where the TREE is visible, so its locators are the assertion surface for the depth-3 spec: a `line(index)` locator, a `speciesOf(lineIndex)` list, a `varietiesOf(lineIndex, speciesIndex)` list, plus the per-entry Change and Remove links at EACH depth. Get the nesting of the locators right and the feature spec below becomes readable; get it wrong and it becomes a pile of nth-child selectors.
NEW. The bulk-details variant page in the spoke-3 page set (§2.1). Locate and cover whatever the built page collects; do not invent fields.

NEW. Spoke 4 (§2.1, `sections/additional-details.js`): `totalGrossWeight` (mandatory), `grossVolume` (optional), `grossVolumeUnit` (required IFF grossVolume is answered — a `presentGate`). That conditional is the interesting behaviour here and `additional-details.spec.ts` must pin it in both directions.

ADD `answerCommodities(options)` and `answerAdditionalDetails(options)` to the flow created at pp-062, keeping the established fill/save/answer split.

`answerCommodities()` walks: hub → spoke 3 → input method (MANUAL) → search and pick a code → basic description → species/varieties → summary → return to the hub. Parameterise it enough for the depth-3 spec to drive it (how many lines, how many species per line, how many varieties per species) WITHOUT the spec reaching into page objects itself — that is what keeps the depth-3 spec readable as a statement about the tree rather than a click script.

NEW. Per-page specs for the spoke-3 pages: input method (render, both options, validation, and — the assertion that matters — `commodity.inputMethod` PERSISTS, unlike `importType`); search (results, no-results state, picking a code); basic description (nine fields, validation per field, save-and-continue); bulk details. Each with back-link and resume coverage.

Every persisted assertion goes through `plantProductsApi.load(ref)` against the real backend: `commodityCode` is the CODE and `commodityDescription` is the ref-data-derived text, not something the user typed.

NEW. The species/varieties page: `eppoCode` and `genusAndSpecies` are mandatory; varieties are OPTIONAL (no minEntries — §3.1); `varietyClass` is allow-listed per species and is NULL when not applicable — assert the null case, not just the happy one, because an allow-list that silently accepts an inapplicable class is invisible in the UI.

Assert `variety` persists as the ID, not the display label (Open Q 2 ruling). This is a one-line assertion that catches a whole class of ref-data mistake and cannot be made from the UI alone.

NEW. Spoke 4: `totalGrossWeight` mandatory; `grossVolumeUnit` required IFF `grossVolume` is answered, and NOT required when it is blank — both directions. Numeric validation on each. Persisted values assert as numbers, not strings.

NEW — THE MOST IMPORTANT SPEC IN THE PLANT SUITE, and the cross-repo counterpart of P-7 / pp-012's in-repo characterisation test.

THE SCENARIO, in one spec so the tree is asserted as a whole:
1. Add commodity LINE A; under it add SPECIES A1 and SPECIES A2; under SPECIES A1 add VARIETY A1a and VARIETY A1b.
2. Add commodity LINE B with its own species.
3. Assert the summary page renders the full tree at all three depths, with the right entries under the right parents.
4. REMOVE A MIDDLE ENTRY — species A1 (which has children), and separately variety A1a — and assert (a) the remaining tree is correct at every depth, (b) removing a parent removed its children and did NOT orphan them onto a sibling, (c) no other line was disturbed.
5. Assert the PERSISTED document after every mutation: `commodity.commodityComplement[].species[].varieties[]` matches the on-screen tree exactly, with `uniqueComplementId` stable across saves for lines that were not touched.

WHY THIS SPEC EXISTS (FD-9 / P-7): depth 3 is UNPROVEN in the engine — the live exemplar `animalIdentifiers` is depth 2. The frontend has an in-repo characterisation test for the engine mechanics, but this repo is the only place the whole chain (UI → engine scope/wipe → mapper → real backend → Mongo → reload) is exercised. Index-shifting on removal is the classic failure: it looks right on screen and is wrong in the document, or vice versa. Assert BOTH SIDES on EVERY mutation — a spec that checks only the DOM would have passed through the entire class of bug this is written for.

Tag it `@integration` if it needs the integration lane's real-mode target; otherwise leave it untagged so it runs in the default plant project. Do NOT invent a set tag (pp-060: sets are projects, tags stay orthogonal).

increments.notes:
THE TESTS REPO IS A SEPARATE GIT REPO — own remote, own branch (`spike/trace-to-requirements`), own CI, own package.json. Do not assume the frontend's npm scripts. Verbatim: "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"; "lint": "eslint ."; "format:check": "prettier --check '**/*.{ts,js,mjs,md,json,yml,yaml}'"; "test"; "test:local"; "test:a11y"; plus `test:plant-products` from pp-060.

DEPTH 3 IS THE FIRST OF ITS KIND IN THIS SERVICE. FD-9 models commodities as `commodityLines → species → varieties`; the live exemplar `animalIdentifiers` is depth 2, so the engine's scope/wipe/completeness machinery has never run three levels deep in production code. P-7 / pp-012 pins the engine mechanics in the frontend repo. THIS increment is the only place the full chain runs — browser DOM, engine, set-owned mapper, real REST backend, Mongo, reload — and the only place index-shifting on removal can be caught in both representations at once.

ASSERT BOTH SIDES, ALWAYS. The failure that matters looks correct in exactly one representation: the summary page renders the right tree while the document has a variety hanging off the wrong species, or vice versa. A spec that asserts only the DOM, or only the API response, passes through it. Every mutation in `commodity-depth-3.spec.ts` gets a DOM assertion and an API assertion.

REAL CANNED DATA ONLY: commodity codes, EPPO codes, varieties and classes come from `domain/plant-products/constants/*` (pp-061), which in turn transcribes the frontend set's real fixture services. An invented EPPO code will pass typecheck, drive the UI, and then fail an allow-listed gate in a way that reads as a service bug.

DEPENDS ON pp-028 (frontend commodities build) and pp-012 (the in-repo depth-3 characterisation test). If pp-012 has not landed, do not write this spec as a substitute for it — a red engine mechanic should fail fast in a unit test, not after a five-minute browser walk.

ROLLBACK: `git stash push -u`, never `reset --hard` + `clean -fd`.
openQuestions: Whether the built commodity pages expose per-entry Remove controls at every depth or only at the summary. Planned resolution: locate what exists and cover it; if removal at species or variety level is only reachable one way, say so in the spec rather than skipping the removal case — removal is the half of the depth-3 contract most likely to be wrong.

Whether `speciesId` round-trips through the UI at all (§3.1 calls it 'optional, transient-ish'). Planned resolution: assert whatever the document actually carries after a save-reload cycle and record it; do not assert an expected value derived from the plan when the plan itself flags the field as unsettled.

increments.notes: 1:1 carry of inc-022 (page spec goods-movement-services.json — adversarially re-verified; the page is DATA capture, not a GVMS/NCTS integration). EXEMPLARS pinned live this session: sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js (equalsGate signature + reasons-object shape + purge-on-flip comment idiom), features/import-reason/controller.js (single-page collecting idiom), features/contact/template.njk (govukRadios macro usage), features/commodities/evaluation.js:51 (binding convert idiom). DECISIONS (headless): (1) TWO-TIER COLLAPSED — legacy lets you save the page with both questions blank and only blocks at backend submission (@NotNull on provideCtcMrn/isGVMSRoute); the spec flags this as a policy choice, and pp-009 records the set as single-layer Joi-voice, so both radios are required at the point of answer, adopting the legacy submission strings 'Select if using the Common Transit Convention (CTC)' / 'Select if using the Goods Vehicle Movement Service (GVMS)' as the page errors; (2) MRN error = the single canonical 'Enter a valid Movement Reference Number' for empty/length/pattern (c-018 one string per field; matches the legacy LIVE wiring — the two more-specific legacy strings are dead copy there); regex copied verbatim /^\d{2}[A-Za-z0-9]{16}$/ with trim-before-validate (legacy trims too); (3) caption 'Transport' kept spec-verbatim even though goods-movement is its own hub spoke — spokes 5 and 6 are both transport-family and mirror-existing wins over inventing a new caption; (4) enum + boolean normalisation: CTC stored as ADD_MRN_NOW|ADD_MRN_LATER|NO, usingGvms canonical boolean via binding convert (fixes the legacy value-casing inconsistency and the string-vs-boolean split); (5) MRN as a gated SCALAR obligation with equalsGate — the engine's purge-on-flip exactly reproduces the legacy delete-on-save behaviour (including 'add later' clearing a saved MRN), so no controller-side delete code exists; (6) 'Save and review' change-from-review button variant and etag optimistic concurrency NOT built (house: change-context via kit + whole-document last-write-wins, Open Q 3); (7) legacy per-CHED-type render gates (enableCtcQuestion/enableGvmsQuestion) are dead code for a CHED-PP-only set — both questions render unconditionally; (8) conditional-reveal JS comes from the stock govuk-frontend bundle already loaded by the shared layout — no webpack entry needed. FIXES-NOT-PORTED from the spec's nonStandardPatterns: orphaned CTC hint (confirmed WCAG-relevant defect axe cannot see), href='#' back link with bespoke classes, hand-authored fieldset markup, two-equal-primary-buttons, the global aria-allowed-attr axe suppression (deliberately dropped — scan with the rule ON, including the expanded-reveal and error states legacy never scanned). Check-answers row: features/check-answers does not exist until pp-038 — that increment owns the goods-movement card rows; no omission here. RULINGS APPLIED: c-004 (There is a problem), c-014 family (proper heading structure), c-018 (canonical Joi-voice strings), FD-5/FD-6 (set-owned records), obligation-field-map inc-022 (goodsMovementServices.* nested DTO object).
openQuestions: Deferred-MRN flow is unmapped: legacy has a separate add_ncts_mrn page (outside the 28-page CHED-PP journey map, never traced) where an 'add later' MRN is presumably captured. RULINGS APPLIED from the traders-addresses page spec: the legacy page's architecture is deliberately NOT ported — (a) mini-hub-inside-a-form with hidden etag → a normal collecting page in the house model (no etag; last-write-wins per Open Q 3); (b) four-column trader-tables with bespoke col-*/trader-table/table-responsive CSS → govuk-summary-list per populated party (the spec's own govukAlternative); (c) empty-slot placeholder tables (screen-reader-meaningless, shown to pass axe while defective) → no table when empty; (d) the 'Same as consignee' link-button (no double-click guard, wrong label — it copies the IMPORTER, one-shot irreversible) → the spec's recommended Radios question naming the importer honestly, which also makes the choice reversible; (e) two equal-weight primary buttons → house single-primary + shared save actions; (f) legacy slot-level messages ('Add a delivery address') → per-field Joi messages, since the destination is now collected in-page rather than via a sub-journey. Mandatoriness grounded in legacy PartOne @NotNull evidence (importer/destination/consignor mandatory, packer optional): importer satisfied by POP-1 auto-population (modelled as derived value, exactly as the spec's requiredEvidence note recommends); destination via the gated leaves; consignor deferred to pp-036 (its 'Add a consignor or exporter' enforcement becomes manifest mandatoriness rolling into the traders row, not a controller rule here). destinationSameAsConsignee has no backend field — projected as destination=importer-copy on save (matching the legacy asserted copy behaviour) and re-derived by equality on load; flagged in openQuestions. Destination/packer email+telephone deliberately omitted in pass 1 (legacy sub-journey optionality unverified; §3.1 does not list them) with mapper omission assertions. EXEMPLARS: sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-section.md + add-a-page.md; transport feature group (multi-page group shape); origin feature (conditional scope + service-backed select); regionCode/purposeInInternalMarket obligations (equalsGate status-flip and purge-on-flip decision shapes, model/obligations/helpers/scalar/equals-gate.js verified live this session). ORDERING ASSUMPTION: pp-010 (contract.plant-products.test.js, T-5) precedes all m2+ pages per §9 rule 2 even though it is not in this increment's canonical dependsOn.

increments.notes: AMENDED 2026-08-01 for Sam's ruling R3 (co-residency). ONE substantive change, and it is a build-breaker if missed: THE DASHBOARD IS THE PAGE THE URL NAMESPACE WORK EXISTS FOR. In live-animals, dashboardPath() and createPath() are used BOTH as Hapi route paths (evaluated at module load, when controllers build their route tables) AND as rendered links (evaluated per request) in the SAME file — controller.js:114,126. Under a mount prefix those two uses must produce DIFFERENT strings, which is why pp-057 (P-10) splits shared/paths.js into prefix-free ROUTE-SHAPE builders (pageRoutePath, hubRoutePath, and the two NEW ones dashboardRoutePath() and createRoutePath()) and prefix-bearing LINK builders (pagePath, hubPath, dashboardPath, createPath, breadcrumbs). This increment must use dashboardRoutePath()/createRoutePath() for its two route paths and dashboardPath()/createPath() for its startAction, listAction, redirect, form action and every pagination/sort/filter href. Getting it backwards yields either a route registered at /plant-products/plant-products (page unreachable) or a link that drops the prefix (lands on the live-animals dashboard) — both silent-ish failures that unit tests catch only if you pin them, hence the added acceptance criterion and the prefix-integrity E2E scenario. R7 SHARPENS THIS (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session — symmetric mounts): under the reversed FD-16 the route-shape-vs-link distinction now differs for BOTH sets, not just for plant-products. When live-animals sat at prefix '', its route builders and link builders emitted the SAME string, so the live-animals twin of this file could not demonstrate the difference and a mix-up there was invisible. Now `dashboardRoutePath()` is '/' while `dashboardPath()` is '/live-animals' for that set and '/plant-products' for this one — so the two places in THIS file must each use the correct family and BOTH must be pinned by assertion, exactly as §4.6 A row 8 requires of the live-animals twin (sets/live-animals/.../features/dashboard/controller.js:114,126 — mirror it). Second consequence: the plant dashboard renders at /plant-products, NOT at /. Under R7 the root belongs to NEITHER set — it is a server-wide 302 to /live-animals (FD-18) — and the live-animals dashboard lives at /live-animals; the dashboard e2e spec carries the co-residency canary asserting all three in one run. All SERVED_SET framing is deleted — there is no served-set env var (ruling R3); PLANT_PRODUCTS_MODE selects the plant records stub and nothing else. Everything else below is unchanged by the reversal. ORIGINAL NOTES FOLLOW. Completes the pp-007 m0 dashboard skeleton to the full inc-028 build. No recipe covers dashboards (SIBLING-SET-PLAN §8 G-G) — the plan is an exemplar transposition of sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/ (controller.js's renderDashboard/query-parsing/pagination shape, notification-helper.js, view-model/row + sort-options, buildPageResultsRangeLabel's singular/plural/empty handling), verified live this session. Rulings applied: c-026 (real optgroups on the country select, data shipped by pp-013), c-027 (one GDS-sentence-case status vocabulary shared by tags and filter — implemented as view-model/statuses.js so both surfaces read one map), c-012 ('Republic of Ireland'), c-018 (one canonical validation string per rule; the legacy '"Search" must be 255 characters or less' quoted-label defect is not inherited). FD-13: the dashboard page is already inside the flow 'start' section from pp-007 — no flow.js/task-rows/entry-guard change, hence flowChanges {}. AMENDED FOR RULING R7 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session) — SYMMETRIC MOUNTS. The 'testDir/path split against the same server' description now applies SYMMETRICALLY: the live-animals journeys project's specs and its e2e/live-animals-journey.js helper are ALSO prefixed (pp-057 migrated them under §4.6 D, which the round-2 plan missed entirely), so this increment writes its plant equivalents prefixed FROM THE START rather than inventing the pattern. Concretely: e2e/plant-products-journey.js's BASE is '/plant-products' and e2e/live-animals-journey.js's is '/live-animals' — neither is ''; both helpers front-anchor their journey-id regex on their own base; and both journeys projects share the SAME HOST-ONLY baseURL, because a set-prefixed baseURL would break /health, /signout and /public/* and hide the other set. A bare page.goto('/') anywhere in the plant helper now 302s to /live-animals (FD-18) and silently runs the journey in the wrong set — call that out in review.

CROSS-REPO DEPENDENCY (R8): this increment is the IN-REPO whole-journey proof and it runs against the plant RECORDS STUB in a self-hosted server. It is NOT the cross-repo one. The whole-journey coverage against the real workspace stack — real backend, real Mongo, real OIDC — is pp-065 in repos/trade-imports-animals-tests, together with the set-neutral co-residency spec that can only exist there. Do not treat this increment as discharging that; §9 constraint 17 makes the tests-repo increment part of the milestone's definition of done.

AMENDED 2026-08-01 for Sam's ruling R3 (co-residency) — RETITLED, because the word 'split' carried a false premise. The round-1 framing assumed TWO SERVERS: one booted for live-animals, one booted with SERVED_SET=plant-products, with the whole-journey suites split between them. With one server serving both sets, the e2e split is a testDir/baseURL-PATH split only — same Playwright webServer, same port, same process; the plant journeys project just drives the /plant-products path-space. Consequences applied above: the helper's BASE becomes '/plant-products' (and, under R7, the live-animals helper's BASE is '/live-animals' — symmetric, neither empty); the script drops SERVED_SET and keeps PLANT_PRODUCTS_MODE=stub, which selects the plant records stub and nothing else; the webServer block is untouched because pp-011 already added PLANT_PRODUCTS_MODE beside LIVE_ANIMALS_MODE; and the plant-set-only assertion is now a MOUNT proof rather than an env-pass-through proof. NEW — one spec per page landed above: `transport.spec.ts`, `goods-movement.spec.ts`, `contact.spec.ts`, `nominated-contacts.spec.ts`, `documents.spec.ts`, `traders.spec.ts`, `consignor.spec.ts`, `review.spec.ts`, `declaration.spec.ts`, `confirmation.spec.ts`.

EACH covers the same five things: renders with the right heading and fields; valid save returns to the hub and updates the row status; each mandatory field missing produces an error-summary entry LINKED to its field; the back link returns to the hub; a saved answer is present on re-entry (real backend resume). Persisted values assert through `plantProductsApi.load(ref)` as CODES/ENUMS, not labels.

Per-page specifics worth naming: `transport.spec.ts` must assert that changing the BCP CHANGES the available inspection premises (the allow-list is lazily resolved per gate execution — a cached option list is the defect); `goods-movement.spec.ts` must assert the MRN field is required only under ADD_MRN_NOW and NOT under the other two.

NEW — THE ASSURANCE FOR §2.1's 12-SPOKE MAPPING, and the direct mirror of the live-animals spec of the same name (`tests/e2e/features/live-animals/hub-groups-and-cya-rows.spec.ts`).

ASSERT:
1. Every spoke appears under the right numbered GROUP heading, in the order §2.1 gives: 1 Origin of the import, 2 Purpose, 3 Commodity, 4 Additional details, 5 Transport to the BCP, 6 Goods movement services, 7 Contact details, 8 Nominated contacts, 9 Accompanying documents, 10 Traders, 11 Billing, 12 Review and submit.
2. Each row's STATUS changes as its section is completed (Not started → In progress → Completed).
3. Spoke 8 (Nominated contacts) is OPTIONAL and does NOT gate readiness — leave it empty and still reach review.
4. Spoke 11 (Billing) is CONDITIONAL (`conditional: true`, c-007) and is HIDDEN at m4 — assert it is absent, and note in the spec that m5 flips this.
5. Spoke 12 (Review and submit) is NOT a task row (FD-12) — it is the authored gate `scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers` — and it unlocks ONLY when every mandatory row is Completed. Assert both states: locked with one mandatory row outstanding, unlocked when none is.
6. Every CYA row on the review page maps to a spoke, and its Change link returns to the page that owns the answer and then back to the review page.

ASSERT THE FULL RENDERED LIST, dividers and separators included — do not filter visual elements out of the option/row assertions to make them tidy.

NEW. Pins the c-015 floor: with ZERO accompanying documents the spoke-9 row is not Completed and review does not unlock; with ONE it is and it does. Also assert removing the last document takes it back to incomplete — a minEntries floor that only works on the way up is a common half-implementation.

NEW. ASSERT, all in ONE browser context:
1. `GET /` responds 302 (NOT 301 — FD-18 is explicit: a 301 is cached indefinitely and would be painful to unpick when a picker page replaces the redirect) and lands the browser on `/live-animals`.
2. Start a LIVE-ANIMALS journey and a PLANT-PRODUCTS journey in the SAME context. Both drafts progress independently.

THE CO-RESIDENCY SPEC IS THE POINT OF THIS INCREMENT. The frontend has an in-repo `co-residency.test.js` that boots one server with both gateways — but on STUBS, in-process, with no browser, no cookie jar and no OIDC. Everything that co-residency actually risks in production is browser-shaped: two cookie jars in one context, two mount prefixes on one origin, server-wide routes that must not have drifted under a prefix. Only this repo can assert any of it.

THE COOKIE ASSERTION IS THE ONE PEOPLE WILL WANT TO DROP because it reaches into the browser context rather than the DOM. Keep it. FD-3 made per-set cookie names load-bearing rather than cosmetic precisely because both sets' sessions are live in the same browser at the same time, and §4.6 A row 4 records that live-animals' journey cookie path MOVES from `/` to `/live-animals` under R7 (invalidating existing sessions — accepted). A cookie left at path `/` still works in every single-set spec and silently lets one set clobber the other's session.

302, NOT 301 — assert the status code, not just the destination. FD-18 chose 302 deliberately: a 301 is cached by browsers indefinitely and would be painful to unpick when a set-picker page eventually replaces the redirect. A spec that only asserts 'ends up on /live-animals' passes with a 301 and lets the wrong one ship.

`/signout` IS THE TRIPWIRE FOR FD-19. Today `src/server/router.js:20-24` pushes `signout` into the SAME `server.register` array as the live-animals gateway; under R7 that call carries `{ routes: { prefix: '/live-animals' } }`, which would silently move `/signout` to `/live-animals/signout`. The route registers fine either way — unit tests are happy — and only an unprefixed `GET /signout` catches it.

JOURNEY SPECS ARE FLAKY ON A FRESH STACK. Transient 500s in `beforeEach` that recover on retry are a known characteristic here; `shared-config.ts:17` already sets `retries: 1`. A run that is green with flaky journey specs is a PASS. Do not chase it by weakening assertions, and do not raise the worker count — `playwright.e2e.config.ts:22-24` caps local workers at 4 because unbounded workers overwhelm the defra-id auth stub.

Whether the cross-browser lane's WebKit run can complete a plant happy path within the existing timeouts. increments.notes:
THE TESTS REPO IS A SEPARATE GIT REPO — own remote, own branch (`spike/trace-to-requirements`), own CI, own package.json. Verbatim scripts: "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"; "lint": "eslint ."; "format:check": "prettier --check '**/*.{ts,js,mjs,md,json,yml,yaml}'"; "test:a11y": "npm run _clean_and_test -- --grep '@a11y'"; "test:docker-compose:a11y"; "test": "npm run _assert_stack && npm run _clean && npm run database:reseed && npm run _test_e2e". There is no frontend a11y script to borrow.

STANDING RULE — A GREEN AXE SCAN IS NOT SUFFICIENT EVIDENCE ON ITS OWN. The CHED-PP trace work recorded real defects on these very pages that axe cannot see, and this suite must not be presented as proof they are absent:
- THREE controls sharing the accessible name 'Copy' on the review/notification surface, with nothing distinguishing which reference each one acts on, and a fourth in a state the traces never captured (`workareas/shared/trace-requirements/ched-pp/pages/review-notification.json`). Duplicate accessible names on distinct actions pass axe and defeat a screen-reader user completely.
- A link that announces as a same-page link when it is not, plus a bespoke `--next-to-breadcrumbs` modifier reaching into a govuk component's own CSS namespace (`.../pages/csv-upload.json:115`) — custom CSS inside a component namespace also blocks clean govuk-frontend upgrades.
- The legacy service's own a11y suite scanned its review page ONLY in the DRAFT state (`review-notification.json`), so the submitted/checks/split states were never covered.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS INCREMENT: cover every STATE (that is why the initial/filled/error/view-states split exists), and when a page ships a repeated action name or a bespoke component modifier, say so in the spec as a comment naming the trace finding — an automated pass on a page with a known axe-invisible defect is a misleading green, not assurance. Where a defect is real, it belongs in a ticket, not in an exclusion.

STAY INSIDE THE GOVUK-FRONTEND TOOLBOX. If a plant page needs a visual fix to pass a scan, the fix is a govuk-* component or utility class in the frontend repo, not custom CSS — and it is a frontend increment, not a spec exclusion here.

NEW. The plant analogue of `flows/live-animals/notification-actions.ts`. Drives the dashboard row actions and the action pages: `view(ref)`, `amend(ref)`, `cancelAmend(ref)`, `copy(ref)`, `delete(ref)`, plus the confirm/cancel steps each of them lands on.

NEW. The state machine, end to end against the real backend, seeded through `flows/plant-products/api-journey.ts` (pp-061) so no case re-walks 12 spokes.

CASES, each asserting BOTH the rendered state and `plantProductsApi.load(ref)`:
1. DRAFT resume — an API-seeded draft opens at `/plant-products/notifications/{ref}`, the hub shows the seeded rows' statuses, and continuing from a spoke saves onto the same document.
2. SUBMIT — a complete seeded draft submits; `status: 'SUBMITTED'` (`PUT …/{ref}/status`, §6.2 `finalise`).
3. AMEND — a submitted notification enters amend; `status: 'AMEND'`; edits are visible in the working document.
4. CANCEL-AMEND — discards the edits and returns to `status: 'SUBMITTED'` with the SUBMITTED BASELINE restored (§6.2: `{ status: 'SUBMITTED', discardChanges: true }`, D-4). Assert the edit is GONE, not merely that the status flipped — a status-only assertion passes on a cancel that forgot to restore.
5. VIEW — the read-only view of a submitted notification renders its values and offers no edit affordance.

Mirrors `tests/e2e/features/live-animals/promoted-lifecycle.spec.ts` in intent; write it fresh against the plant document.

NEW. The UI half of cancel-amend — the confirm page, its copy, the No/Cancel path leaving the amend in progress, and the Yes path discarding.

THE R7 ASSERTION THAT MATTERS: after confirming, the redirect lands under `/plant-products`, front-anchored. The live-animals equivalent redirects to a literal `'/'` (`sets/live-animals/.../features/cancel-amend/controller.test.js:104`), and pp-045 changes the PLANT equivalents to `dashboardPath()`. A plant controller that kept a bare `'/'` would now hit the FD-18 302 and drop the user into the LIVE-ANIMALS dashboard — a silent cross-set leak that renders a perfectly normal-looking page. Assert `^/plant-products`, never just 'not an error'.

The live-animals equivalents to mirror in intent: `delete-notification/controller.test.js:56,80,83` (`noHref: '/'`, two `redirect: '/'`) and `tests/e2e/features/live-animals/notification-delete.spec.ts`.

NEW — and the ONLY end-to-end proof of the copy idempotency contract (R4, §6.2 `copy` row).

CASES:
1. Copy a submitted notification → a NEW DRAFT with a NEW `GBN-PP-…` reference, DOCUMENTLESS (accompanying documents are deliberately not copied — D-19), content otherwise carried over.
2. IDEMPOTENCY: the Copy button carries a `randomUUID()` minted per RENDERED action in a hidden input named `idempotencyKey`, sent as the `Idempotency-Key` header. Submitting the SAME rendered form twice (double-click, or a re-POST of the captured form) yields ONE new draft, not two. This is the assertion the whole R4 sequencing exists for and it cannot be made anywhere else — the frontend's stub records the key, but only the real backend enforces it.
3. SCOPED TO THE SOURCE REFERENCE: the same idempotency key against a DIFFERENT source reference DOES create a new draft. A backend that dedupes on the key alone passes case 2 and fails here.
4. RE-RENDER MINTS A NEW KEY: reloading the page and copying again DOES create a second draft — otherwise the button is dead after one use.
5. THE R7 BOUNDARY: after copying, the redirect lands under `^/plant-products` and the new draft opens at `/plant-products/notifications/{newRef}`. Never `'/'`, never live-animals.

NOTE THE TRANSPOSITION (§6.2): live-animals implements idempotency on the FULFILMENT resource (`POST /fulfilments/{id}/copy`, `adapters/http/notification-api-client.ts:51-55`); plant-products puts `/copies` on the NOTIFICATION resource (`POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies`). Transpose the pattern, not the path.

Add `plantProductsNotificationActions`, constructed from `plantProductsPages` (mirroring the live-animals `notificationActions` fixture at `:33-35`). Keep it beside the live-animals one; do not collapse them.

Add whatever action-surface locators these specs need and pp-064 did not: the dashboard row's action menu (View / Amend / Copy / Delete), the delete-confirmation page, the cancel-amend confirmation page, and — importantly — the Copy form's HIDDEN `idempotencyKey` input, which `copy-as-new.spec.ts` must read and re-submit to prove case 2.

The Copy button's form action and post-copy redirect are PREFIX-BEARING LINKS (built from `pagePath` / `hubPath` / `dashboardPath`), not route shapes — pp-055 says the same thing on the frontend side. So the form's `action` attribute should read `/plant-products/notifications/…`; assert that attribute directly in the spec. A bare `/notifications/…` action would post into nothing (or, worse, into whatever the other set serves).

increments.notes:
THE TESTS REPO IS A SEPARATE GIT REPO — own remote, own branch (`spike/trace-to-requirements`), own CI, own package.json. Verbatim scripts: "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"; "lint": "eslint ."; "format:check": "prettier --check '**/*.{ts,js,mjs,md,json,yml,yaml}'"; "test": "npm run _assert_stack && npm run _clean && npm run database:reseed && npm run _test_e2e"; "test:local": "npm run test:integration"; plus `test:plant-products` from pp-060. Do not assume the frontend's scripts.

WHY THE R7 BOUNDARY ASSERTIONS ARE THE HEART OF THIS INCREMENT. Live-animals redirects to a literal `'/'` after delete, cancel-amend and copy — verified in the frontend at `delete-notification/controller.test.js:56,80,83`, `cancel-amend/controller.test.js:104`, `notification-actions/controller.test.js:132` and `dashboard/controller.test.js:403`. pp-045 changes the PLANT equivalents to `dashboardPath()`. If any plant controller keeps a bare `'/'`, FD-18's server-wide 302 forwards the user to `/live-animals` and they land in a fully-rendered, entirely wrong set's dashboard. Nothing errors. No log line. The only thing that catches it is a front-anchored URL assertion on every post-action redirect — which is why every one of these specs carries one, and why 'the page loaded' is never an acceptable assertion here.

WHY API-SEEDED, NOT UI-WALKED: reaching AMEND through the UI means completing 12 spokes and submitting, per case. `flows/plant-products/api-journey.ts` (pp-061) exists so lifecycle coverage costs seconds rather than minutes and so a lifecycle failure is attributable to the lifecycle, not to some unrelated page's validation.

COPY IDEMPOTENCY IS ONLY PROVABLE HERE. The engine port already carries the key (`engine/journey.js:125` `copyJourney(request, h, journeyId, idempotencyKey)`), the frontend mints a `randomUUID()` per rendered action into a hidden `idempotencyKey` input, and the set's `records/real.js` sends it as the `Idempotency-Key` header. The frontend's stub mirrors it with a dedupe key — but a stub proves the frontend sends the key, not that the SERVICE honours it. Only a real POST to `POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies` does. The three-case bar (same form twice = one draft; same key + different source = new draft; re-render = new key = new draft) is what distinguishes a real idempotency implementation from a backend that dedupes on the key alone or a frontend that reuses one key forever.

SOFT DELETE, NOT HARD. §6.2: `softDelete` is `PUT …/{ref}/status` `{ status: 'DELETED' }` and is idempotent; `list` hides DELETED server-side. A spec that asserts a 404 after delete is asserting a contract the service does not have and will fail for the right-looking wrong reason.

DEPENDS ON pp-045 (the frontend draft-lifecycle build) and pp-055 (copy idempotency on the plant records port). Both must have landed — R4 sequences the idempotency work BEFORE the Copy button ships, and this is the increment that proves the sequencing worked.

increments.recipe: No recipe. filesToTouch.what: Make a malformed status-change body produce 400, not 500. DIAGNOSE FIRST — do not assume the site. Observed: PUT /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/status with {"status": null} returns 500 over the real HTTP stack; a literal-null body and a missing body do the same. The reporting implementor's read was that processing fails before bean validation can produce a 400, which points at StatusChangeRequest deserialisation or the controller's argument binding rather than at the service. RECONCILE THE MISLEADING SLICE. This @WebMvcTest currently asserts 'missing status -> 400' and PASSES, while the real application returns 500 — so the slice is not representative of production and is giving false confidence. Establish WHY (the slice almost certainly loads a different exception-handling stack than the full context does), then either make the slice representative or move the assertion to the IT layer where it is actually proved. Do not simply delete it. Whatever is decided, no test may be left claiming behaviour the running application does not exhibit.

Restore the null-status assertion that pp-004 removed as out-of-scope, now that production returns 400. Assert over the real HTTP stack that a null status, a literal-null body and a missing body each return 400 with the problem-style body — all three were observed returning 500.

acceptanceCriteria: PUT /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/status with {"status": null} returns 400, proved by an integration test over the real HTTP stack (not only a @WebMvcTest slice).

So pp-004 removed the assertion and this increment owns it. Evidence: logs/pp-004-focused-verify.log line 1136 — 'AssertionError: Status expected:<400 BAD_REQUEST> but was:<500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR>', 21 of 22 new plant ITs passing.

THE SECOND FINDING IS THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE. pp-003's controller slice asserts 'missing status -> 400' and passes, while the full stack returns 500. A slice test that passes where production fails is false confidence, and pp-003 shipped a whole package of controller slices built the same way — so whatever explains this one probably applies to the others. Treat 'why did the slice pass' as the real deliverable of this increment; the 400 fix itself is small.

increments.recipe: No recipe. The fix shape is whatever pp-054 landed for the plant-products equivalent — read that first and transpose it back, so the two implementations converge again rather than diverging further.

filesToTouch.what: The live-animals fulfilment-copy idempotency path. Same defect pp-054's review found in the transposed plant-products copy: the duplicate-key recovery lookup runs inside the same @Transactional method whose insert has just thrown DuplicateKeyException. MongoTransactionManager is registered unconditionally (animals/configuration/MongoConfig.java:91), so this IS a real Mongo transaction and the server-side duplicate-key error can end it — meaning the concurrent loser's recovery read executes through an aborted session and fails, instead of returning the existing copy with 201. Apply the same restructure pp-054 used: keep the single-document insert and its recovery out of the aborted transaction, or recover in a fresh transaction after rollback.

Add a genuinely concurrent integration test over the real HTTP stack: two simultaneous fulfilment-copy requests with the same Idempotency-Key against the same source, both returning 201 with identical body and Location, and exactly one document persisted. Use a CountDownLatch or equivalent so the requests actually overlap. The existing coverage does NOT reach this path — the replay test is sequential and the unit test mocks a successful post-exception lookup, which proves the catch block compiles rather than that the contract holds.

specs: IT: two concurrent fulfilment-copy requests sharing an Idempotency-Key both return 201 with the same body and Location, and exactly one document exists afterwards.
The existing sequential replay behaviour, the unique partial index behaviour, and missing/blank header rejection are all unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: The duplicate-key recovery lookup can no longer execute inside a transaction aborted by the failed insert.

A genuinely concurrent IT proves the losing request returns the existing copy with 201 rather than an error, with exactly one document persisted. A Mockito-fabricated post-exception lookup does not satisfy this criterion.
The live-animals and plant-products idempotency implementations are behaviourally aligned again, restoring Sam's R4 ruling that the two match.
No behaviour change to the sequential replay path, the partial unique index, or header validation.
mvn verify is green end to end, including every pre-existing animals test.
increments.notes:
RAISED DURING THE BUILD (orchestrator, 2026-08-01), not by the planners, and it is a defect in ALREADY-SHIPPED live-animals code rather than in anything this programme wrote. Found by transposition: pp-054 copied the animals idempotency scheme per Sam's ruling R4 ('match live-animals exactly'), and reviewing the copy surfaced a flaw that had gone unnoticed in the original. The orchestrator independently verified the premise before acting — MongoTransactionManager is a plain unconditional @Bean at animals/configuration/MongoConfig.java:91 and the copy method is @Transactional, so there genuinely is a transaction to abort.

WHY IT CARRIES A GATE: this edits shipped live-animals production code on a path that is exercised in a real deployment, and the failure it fixes is a race that current tests do not reach. That combination — shipped code, concurrency, no existing coverage of the path — is worth a human look before it lands, which is why the increment halts for review rather than landing autonomously.

WHY pp-054 DID NOT JUST FIX BOTH: pp-054's scope is the plant-products package. Reaching into animals from a plant-products increment would have put a concurrency change to shipped code inside a diff nobody was reviewing for that, and R4 alignment is restored by this increment instead. The R4 deviation is deliberate and is recorded in WHEN-YOURE-BACK.md: R4 means 'do not invent a different scheme', not 'faithfully reproduce a concurrency bug'.

SCOPE FENCE: the idempotency recovery path and its test coverage. Do not refactor the surrounding fulfilment service, and do not change the sequential replay semantics.
openQuestions: Is the same aborted-transaction recovery pattern used anywhere else in the animals package — any other @Transactional method that catches DuplicateKeyException and then reads? If so this is a class of bug rather than one instance, and the fix should sweep them together.
Does this need a Jira ticket in its own right, given it is a defect in shipped code rather than programme work? The orchestrator's view is yes, but that is Sam's call and no ticket has been raised.

increments.title: Backend (live-animals): malformed request bodies return 500 instead of 400 — GlobalExceptionHandler's RuntimeException catch-all swallows framework exceptions
increments.recipe: No recipe. pp-068 fixed the identical defect in the plant-products package — read PlantProductsExceptionHandler and its commit e2fbdaf first and transpose that shape, so the two handlers stay aligned.

filesToTouch.what: A malformed JSON body returns 500 instead of 400. Proved against the real HTTP stack during pp-068: a malformed POST /notifications returns 500. ROOT CAUSE, established in pp-068 and expected to be the same here: the handler carries a RuntimeException catch-all that intercepts Spring's own HttpMessageNotReadableException — which the framework would otherwise resolve to 400 — and maps it to 500. Handle unreadable bodies explicitly, ahead of the catch-all, returning the house problem-style 400 with no stack-trace content. THE CATCH-ALL ITSELF IS THE REAL QUESTION: HttpMessageNotReadableException is not special, it is merely the instance we caught. Any Spring framework exception that extends RuntimeException — unsupported media type, method not allowed, missing parameter, type mismatch — is liable to the same downgrade to 500. Enumerate which ones the catch-all currently swallows and fix the class of problem, not only the one instance.

Prove the corrected behaviour over the real HTTP stack for every endpoint family that accepts a body — notifications, fulfilment and the document sub-resource: a malformed body, a literal-null body and a missing body each return 400 with the problem-style shape. Assert at the integration layer, NOT only in a @WebMvcTest slice — the whole reason this defect survived is that a slice proved the opposite.

Audit the animals @WebMvcTest slices for the same incomplete-context defect pp-068 found in plant-products: a slice that omits GlobalExceptionHandler exercises Spring's default exception resolution rather than production's, so its status-code assertions can be green while production is broken. Report how many assertions run on the incomplete stack and make the slices representative. Do not delete assertions to resolve a contradiction — a slice and an IT disagreeing means production is wrong, or the slice is.

specs: IT: a malformed JSON body returns 400 with the problem-style shape and no stack-trace content, on every animals endpoint family that accepts a body.
IT: a literal-null body and a missing body each return 400 rather than 500.
Any other Spring framework RuntimeException the catch-all was downgrading now maps to its correct status.
acceptanceCriteria: A malformed request body returns 400, not 500, proved by integration tests over the real HTTP stack for every animals endpoint family that accepts a body.

The GlobalExceptionHandler RuntimeException catch-all no longer downgrades framework exceptions that have a correct status of their own. The set of exceptions it was swallowing is enumerated in the commit message.

The animals @WebMvcTest slices load the same exception-handling stack as production, so a slice can no longer be green where the application is broken. The number of assertions previously running on the incomplete stack is reported.
No existing behaviour changes for well-formed requests: every pre-existing animals unit test and IT still passes without its assertions being edited.
mvn verify is green end to end.
increments.notes:
RAISED DURING THE BUILD (orchestrator, 2026-08-01) — a defect in ALREADY-SHIPPED live-animals code, found by transposition for the second time tonight. pp-068 fixed the identical bug in the plant-products package and, while proving the root cause, probed the animals endpoints and found a malformed POST /notifications returns 500 there too. The pp-068 increment's own text asserted that animals already handled this case correctly; that assertion was wrong, which is worth remembering when a plan claims the incumbent implementation is sound.

WHY IT CARRIES A GATE: it changes exception handling on shipped API surface, and the fix's blast radius is deliberately wider than one endpoint — narrowing a catch-all changes the status code of anything it was previously absorbing. That is exactly the change a human should look at before it lands.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE 400: the catch-all is the defect. HttpMessageNotReadableException is just the instance that surfaced, and any framework RuntimeException with a meaningful status of its own is liable to the same downgrade. A client currently cannot distinguish 'your request was malformed' from 'the server broke', on shipped API surface.

SEE ALSO pp-069, the other shipped-animals defect found the same way. Both were invisible until a second implementation was built beside the first and reviewed harder than the original ever was.
openQuestions: Does the animals handler downgrade other framework exceptions too — unsupported media type, method not allowed, missing request parameter, argument type mismatch? The implementor should enumerate before fixing; if several are affected the increment is larger than 'malformed body' and the title should be corrected.

Do pp-069 and this increment share a root cause worth addressing once — i.e. is there a house pattern for exception handling and transactional boundaries that both packages copied? Worth a look before fixing them independently.
Should these two shipped-code defects be raised as Jira tickets rather than carried in this programme's backlog? The orchestrator's view is yes for both; no ticket has been raised.

revisions.summary: Six rulings applied — the programme re-planned around co-residency, with the add-a-set recipe authored first and copy idempotency pulled forward into m0.
changes: R3 CO-RESIDENCY (the big one) — live-animals and plant-products MUST be servable side by side from ONE Node process. Reverses the boot-time SERVED_SET single-set-per-process decision (SD-9 / FD-1 / FD-2, and FD-4 with them). Sam's reasoning: the L1-L4 architecture was explicitly designed to be set-agnostic — L2 never imports a set, sets arrive via L1 configure* seams, dep-cruiser enforces it — so the blocker is not the design but its implementation, i.e. the module-level singletons and the global URL namespace. The platform work to key the seams by set is now IN SCOPE and scheduled, not deferred: pp-056 (P-9), pp-057 (P-10), pp-058 (P-11), with pp-005, pp-006, pp-007, pp-010 and pp-011 re-planned on top of it. SD-9 rewritten; DV-17 rationale replaced; DV-20 and DV-21 added; the m0 milestone goal, the brief and four sequencing notes rewritten.

R6 ADD-A-SET RECIPE UPFRONT — docs/add-a-set.md is authored BEFORE m0 scaffolding and the scaffold increments then FOLLOW it, as the other recipes are followed. New increment pp-053, placed first in the array. Closes gap G-A by writing the recipe rather than extracting it afterwards; G-A rewritten; SD-15 added.

R4 COPY IDEMPOTENCY — match what live-animals already does, exactly, on both sides, sequenced before the Copy button ships. New increments pp-054 (backend Idempotency-Key on POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies) and pp-055 (frontend records port + contract tests), both m0, both added to pp-045's dependsOn. The one transposition: live-animals implements this on the FULFILMENT resource, the plant-products design puts /copies on the NOTIFICATION resource — transpose the pattern, not the code. SD-16 added.

R1 SD-14 — consignee and importer are TWO SEPARATE MODEL FIELDS, both auto-populated from the acting organisation in pass 1, not one party under two names. Pass-1 behaviour unchanged (both written from stubOrganisationOperator()); model-intent correction only. Already applied to SD-14 before this revision and left untouched here.
R2 — the Lombok @Data/@SuperBuilder domain model with records at API boundaries is CONFIRMED, no change (SD-11 annotated).
R5 — the eleven m5 increments stay UNPLANNED stubs and must not be planned (SD-12 annotated).

revisions.summary: Two rulings applied — R7 makes the two sets' mounts SYMMETRIC (reversing FD-16, so live-animals' URLs change and the tests repo is migrated with them) and R8 puts trade-imports-animals-tests in scope as the programme's third delivery lane with nine increments of its own.
changes: R7 SYMMETRIC MOUNTS — FD-16 is REVERSED. Sam does not accept the asymmetry where live-animals keeps the root and only plant-products is prefixed: 'this stuff is still in development, refactoring live-animals is fine — have them match up; changing URLs if required, just make sure to update the -tests repo as well.' BOTH sets now mount at '/' + setId — /live-animals and /plant-products — and no set owns '/'. Every consequence is planned: FD-18 rules that '/' becomes a server-wide 302 to /live-animals (chosen over a set-picker page and over a 404 because auth/controller.js falls back to '/' in five places and getSafeRedirect only permits relative paths, so a 404 would break OIDC sign-in; 302 not 301 because a 301 is cached indefinitely; no /notifications/* compatibility shim because a shim would have to guess which set a bare journey id belongs to). FD-19 rules that signout is hoisted out of the live-animals register, which would otherwise silently move /signout to /live-animals/signout and break the OIDC sign-out leg with nothing failing. THE ACCEPTANCE BAR THAT DIED WITH FD-16: 'every existing URL assertion passes UNEDITED — that is the proof the root mount is a no-op' is deleted from pp-057 and from the two-sided verification rule, and replaced by an explicit ENUMERATED migration (§4.6 A-D as a ticked checklist) proven by UPDATED, FRONT-ANCHORED assertions in both the frontend and the tests repo. SD-17 added; SD-9 and SD-15 rewritten; DV-20 rewritten; DV-22 added; sequencing notes 3 and 5 rewritten and a cross-repo-pair note added; the m0 milestone goal and the brief rewritten.

R8 TESTS-REPO COVERAGE — the honest finding was that across the round-2 backlog's 58 increments only pp-053 and pp-057 mentioned repos/trade-imports-animals-tests, and only to assert it should not break; there were ZERO increments adding plant-products coverage. Sam asked 'have you got it in the plan to update the -tests repo with all the plants stuff?' and the gap is now closed with nine real increments: pp-059 (branch cut + URL migration, paired with pp-057), pp-060 (per-set tree + per-set Playwright projects), pp-061 (m1 API client, domain models, seeds), pp-062 (m2 coverage), pp-063 (m3 depth-3 commodities), pp-064 (m4 pages + hub/CYA), pp-065 (whole-journey E2E + cross-browser + co-residency spec), pp-066 (a11y suite) and pp-067 (m5 lifecycle via API seed). SD-18 added; DV-23 added; G-J added; a tests-repo-lane sequencing note added; every milestone goal now names its tests-repo closer; the brief and the source array now state that this programme spans THREE repos.

BRANCH PARITY — the tests repo is on spike/EUDPA-288-model-retrofit, not spike/trace-to-requirements. CLAUDE.md rule 2 requires cross-repo branches to share a name, so cutting spike/trace-to-requirements in that repo is the explicit FIRST step of pp-059 and no tests-repo change may land before it.

STALE R7 WORDING SWEPT FROM THE INCREMENT FILES — pp-029 asserted that live-animals 'keeps its root-mounted hub'; pp-007, pp-017, pp-018, pp-019, pp-020, pp-023 and pp-041 told their Playwright specs never to hit 'a root-mounted URL, which under co-residency is the live-animals set'; pp-034's sibling-safety clause read 'every live-animals URL byte-identical' with no baseline.
